nodeData.topic: Day 01 · Inquiry, the Vedas and the Gita
nodeData.note: Bg 2.27, 4.3, 18.66; SB 2.3.18 · a class by HH Bhakti Padma Saurabha Pracharaka Swami. Maharaj opens the course by showing that the wish to inquire is what makes us human, and that every inquiry comes down to two: what is the goal of life, and why do I suffer although I try so hard to be happy? He then explains why the senses and reasoning cannot answer these, why the Vedas can, and how the Bhagavad-gita gives their essence. The class ends with how to approach the Gita: through a devotee teacher in a sampradaya, as an inquisitive student. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note:
Maharaj opens the course as a gathering of basic concepts that make the Bhagavad-gita easy to study, and begins with a question to the audience about why they came. His answer is that a burning wish to know sits in their hearts, and this inquisitiveness is the real mark of a human being.

🎙 Maharaj at 02:41 (auto-transcript): “which is really meant for those who like to know what Bhagavad Gita is all about so in the series of the seven days we will be gathering some basic concepts within the Bhagavad Gita by knowing only we can enter into the study of Bhagavad Gita if you know some basic concepts…”

So many handouts and advertisements went out, yet only these people came; they are as busy as everyone else. Maharaj says the underlying reason is a desire to know what this book spoken 5,000 years ago is, why it is respected across nations, religions and castes, and who these Hare Krishnas are that one meets from New York to Russia. — “why only you came, why not others?”

🎙 Maharaj at 03:22 (auto-transcript): “So now we'll start our course with a very important question. The question is that so many handouts have been distributed about this course, so much advertisement has been done about this course, but why only you came, why not others? This is how we start this course. What is…”

Maharaj tells them not to underestimate this quality: the Vedanta-sutra, Vyasa's summary at the end of the Vedas, opens by saying that now is the time to inquire into the Absolute. 'Now' means now that we have crossed so many species and have a human body.

🎙 Maharaj at 06:18 (auto-transcript): “And don't underestimate this quality which you have. The Vedanta Sutras which were written by Vyasa after writing all the Vedic literatures. After writing all the Vedas, Vyasa at the end he wrote one book called Vedanta Sutra. Veda Anta means, Anta means end. At the end of…”

We do inquire all day, about the stock market, the latest movie, the best restaurant in Colombo, but Maharaj says nearly all of it comes down to four needs: food, a place to sleep, security and family life. He cites a Sanskrit verse saying these four are common to humans and animals.

🎙 Maharaj at 08:11 (auto-transcript): “Generally, all of our enquiries in this world are basically restricted to four things. You know what are they? Āhā nidhra bhaibhita nāma chā samānyamita prashipita narādhā dharmohīyekodhippo vishesho dharmēna vihina pashvira samādhā We generally enquire what these four things…”

A dog eats and we eat; we use a dining table and etiquette, but the activity and the satisfaction are the same. Maharaj adds with humour that animals sleep anywhere without arrangements and have no EMIs or family problems, so in some ways they are better off. — “Maximum to maximum you can call ourselves to be sophisticated animals,”

🎙 Maharaj at 10:08 (auto-transcript): “How are we different from animals? Because animals are also into those four things. If you see our dog also eats, we are also eating, the pig also eats, we also eat. You may say, no, no, no, we are eating something very wonderful. We cook our food, we sit on a dining table,…”

Dogs of one street bark at dogs from another; one country's army does the same with guns, and the immigration officer politely asks who you are and why you have come. Family care is there too: the cow looks after her calf.

🎙 Maharaj at 12:24 (auto-transcript): “security you find in the animal kingdom also you have this feeling of security the dogs from other street come to this street to bark I don't know whether you have that kind of thing here but in India in small cities in small towns you have the street dogs are there if other…”

If life is limited to eating, sleeping, mating and defending, the scriptures call such a person a two-legged animal. Maharaj says it is the power of inquiry alone that qualifies us as human.

🎙 Maharaj at 13:58 (auto-transcript): “The Veda says, the scriptures say that if our activities are restricted just for these four things, A, Nidra, Bhaya, Meithun, eating, sleeping, mating and defending, then we are called Dhipada Pashu. Pashu means animal Vipada means what? Two-legged A two-legged animal We…”

A dog and a man walk past the same board announcing a Bhagavad-gita class, but only the man starts thinking. A dog barks at the doorbell without asking who is there; a human asks first and then responds, and so carries the higher responsibility of inquiring into life's purpose.

🎙 Maharaj at 14:35 (auto-transcript): “Just for example you see a board Somebody sees a board of There is a Bhagavad Gita class going on In this particular place in this time A dog also walks It also may see the same board And a human may also see the same world, but the human starts thinking. Manusha, Amanishina,…”

children.topic: First inquiry: the goal of life
children.note:
Maharaj says all inquiries boil down to two, and the first that every human must make is about the goal and purpose of life. The needs of the body are to be met, but they are not the whole purpose.

🎙 Maharaj at 16:29 (auto-transcript): “When we talk of enquiry, there are so many things to enquire about. But all the enquiries boil down to two enquiries. Number one, the goal or the purpose of life. This is the first enquiry everybody has to do. Being born as human being is the first thing which you need to…”

In Mumbai Maharaj once saw a builder's billboard: shabby cracked buildings on one side, a new society with a swimming pool on the other. He takes the slogan one step further and says that more than living, we should be interested in leading our life. — “stop existing, start living.”

🎙 Maharaj at 16:56 (auto-transcript): “There was once I was travelling in Bombay. In Bombay, the builder lobby is very strong. They are very expert in advertising their societies, their constructions and all. A very interesting advertisement I saw. There is a huge billboard, polling, in that there had a mention on…”

The verse from the Second Canto asks whether trees, bellows and village animals do not also live, breathe and eat. Maharaj recalls Srila Prabhupada's example of the ancient banyan tree in the Calcutta botanical gardens: a very long life, but for what use?

Maharaj observes that in chasing a comfortable life people have made living itself harder: long office hours, mothers working to pay for the flat, no time for the family. Even plain living is spoiled, what to speak of leading.

🎙 Maharaj at 19:07 (auto-transcript): “Somehow it has happened because of modernization, because of so much of city life, so much of westernization. What has happened to us? We are just interested in making our living comfortable. But what has happened? In the pursuit of making our life more comfortable, we are…”

Driving without a destination is just driving; leading begins only when there is a goal. Human intelligence is designed for asking what that goal is. — “the importance is leading our life and leading happens only when you have a goal”

🎙 Maharaj at 21:46 (auto-transcript): “Our human life and human intelligence is given not just for living life. Our human intelligence, the speciality of the human being is that there is a goal of life. And it's why leading comes into picture. When you are living, there is no goal. When you are just driving…”

A friend gives a golden pen at a birthday party and the foolish receiver uses it to scratch his head. The pen can do that, but it is meant for writing poetry, and Maharaj says God feels the same when the intelligence He gave is used only for lower purposes. He adds the train passenger who is delighted with his reserved seat but does not know where to get down.

🎙 Maharaj at 22:51 (auto-transcript): “like on your birthday party or some kind of thing your friend or your relative or somebody comes to your house and gives you a gift you see what is a gift, you open in front of them only you are so happy to receive a beautiful pen. It's a golden pen and then this foolish…”

Children are taught to wonder what the star is, but as adults we no longer wonder how plants grow or how the sun rises on time every day. Maharaj plays on the words: we do not wonder, we only wander about looking for better eating, sleeping, mating and defending.

🎙 Maharaj at 25:25 (auto-transcript): “Somehow, the education system, the social situations have made our intelligence so subdued. Though, in the childhood, when the child is sent to the nursery class, he has been taught. I don't know whether this kind of rhymes are taught in Sri Lanka or not. But definitely,…”

children.topic: Second inquiry: why am I suffering?
children.note:
To anyone who finds the goal of life too philosophical, Maharaj offers a second question that nobody can push away: in spite of all my efforts to be happy, why am I suffering? The more we try, the more we seem to suffer.

🎙 Maharaj at 27:06 (auto-transcript): “the second question is very interesting which we all have to enquire the first may be too philosophical the first may be not a very emergency need for you may not experience the emergency in asking this what is the purpose and the goal of life but the second question…”

Maharaj answers the charge of being negative: philosophers everywhere accept that whatever anyone does is done in the hope of happiness. Even money is wanted only because we expect that what it buys will make us happy.

🎙 Maharaj at 28:06 (auto-transcript): “ask question how I can become happy. Rather, everybody wants to become happy. It is said and accepted by all the philosophers around the world. That is, the driving force of all the actions in this world is happiness. Anybody, whatever he does in this world, he does it with…”

Trying to be happy without knowing the cause of suffering is like trying out medicines at the chemist without a diagnosis; it only aggravates the problem. So we try a long holiday and come back bored, or a movie and come out more depressed. The intelligent person first asks for the cause. — “All our pursuits for happiness in this world is exactly like this.”

🎙 Maharaj at 28:43 (auto-transcript): “you know trying to be happy but we are doing a big blunder without trying to know without knowing the cause of suffering if you try to become happy it is like taking a medicine without knowing the disease if you go to the chemist shop and then try out different medicines try…”

Maharaj asks whether our children are really happier than we were; in third standard he did not even know how to spell 'exam'. He tells of a boy who scored 90 percent, missed an entrance exam because he was unwell, and fell into such depression that he could only repeat, 'What will happen to me?'

🎙 Maharaj at 31:01 (auto-transcript): “You really think your parents are more happy and our children are suffering more than we suffered. When I see these children going to the schools and they are burdened with so much of examination, I think of myself when I was studying third standard, I was not even knowing…”

A washerman's overworked donkey goes on strike for a carrot, so the man ties one to a stick on its back, dangling a foot in front of its mouth. Thinking 'one more step', the donkey carries the whole load to the river, and the carrot goes back into the washerman's pocket for the return trip. Maharaj says this is our life.

🎙 Maharaj at 33:30 (auto-transcript): “there is a nice interesting story about happiness. It's like a story which everybody remembers. Even after attending this course, after three years later, people remember, oh, I like this story very much. The story is of a donkey. This donkey was working very hard every day.…”

A 65-year-old man tells Maharaj he will give his life to Krishna after two more years, once his problems are solved. Maharaj asks him what guarantee two more years hold when sixty-five years of youth and energy could not do it. — “still you want two more years to solve your problems?”

🎙 Maharaj at 36:08 (auto-transcript): “Few years back one old man came, he was 65. I was telling him you are already old. Why didn't you take up some responsible services in the temple. Your children are there. They will take care of all these things. Then he told, don't worry, I have banned, give me two more…”

The schoolboy thinks he will be happy in college, the college student when he gets a job and money, the overworked employee when he finds someone who loves him. Each stage brings a new suffering, and Maharaj jokes that after marriage even the hope is gone. Know the cause of suffering, he concludes, and happiness shows itself.

🎙 Maharaj at 37:33 (auto-transcript): “Like a child, he goes to the school. When he goes to the school, every day, morning he has to go to school, whole day he has to listen to the teacher, sometimes shouting, yelling, homework, wear the uniform. Just thinking, this child, when he comes back from school, he sees…”

With the two inquiries fixed, Maharaj explains that knowledge is revealed only to one who asks; otherwise the teacher talks and the students get information, not knowledge. The next question is whom to ask, and for that he describes three sources of knowledge.

🎙 Maharaj at 44:06 (auto-transcript): “These are the two prime inquiries in life. Number one, what is the goal of life and the cause of suffering? Now since we got these two inquiries, when you inquire, what happens? You get knowledge. Knowledge is revealed only to an inquisitive person. What is happening these…”

The first source is knowledge through the senses: I see, so I believe. Maharaj says textbooks, newspapers and television all rest on this, and since the senses themselves are defective, such knowledge carries four defects.

🎙 Maharaj at 45:28 (auto-transcript): “Number one is Pratyksha Praman. In simple words in English we say it as the knowledge attained by sensory perception. I see, I believe. Pratyksha Praman. Perception, knowledge of perception. I see and believe. That means I get knowledge through my senses. There is known as…”

The eye sees only a narrow band between infrared and ultraviolet and cannot see X-rays. Maharaj argues that the very progress of science shows it is incomplete: one scientist calls the atom indivisible, the next divides it, and each theory comes with its own stated limitations. — “If something is complete, why it should progress?”

🎙 Maharaj at 46:24 (auto-transcript): “There are four defects. The first defect is imperfect senses. And you see. You can only see into a limited range between the ultraviolet and the infrared. That is the frequency what you can see. Beyond ultraviolet and infrared you cannot perceive anything like x-rays. Can you…”

A spoon in a glass of water looks bent though it is not, because the eye is prone to illusion. And everyone errs sometimes; even the best authors issue a list of corrections after the book is printed.

🎙 Maharaj at 49:07 (auto-transcript): “is illusion. Like you take a glass of water and put a spoon in it. How does it look like? Bend. If not bend, because our eyes have a tendency to be illusion. These are the second defect lies third effect commit mistakes you may be expert but definitely one day or the other…”

The fourth defect is the tendency to cheat, from the vegetable seller upward. Maharaj recalls a girl who said she liked the advertisements most on TV, and notes that they take a peaceful, satisfied person and convince him that the most useless thing is the most important.

🎙 Maharaj at 49:39 (auto-transcript): “the fourth defect is cheating there's so much of cheating propensity in this world cheating and that whatever information or the knowledge is given to you, it has not this propensity to cheat. That is why when somebody wants to cheat you and somebody is getting cheated, you…”

children.topic: Anumana: reasoning from what we see
children.note:
The second source is inference: the sun looks the size of a football, but intelligence tells us it is far away and bigger than the earth. Since its input is still sense perception, Maharaj says inference is defective too.

🎙 Maharaj at 52:04 (auto-transcript): “Second, it is known as Anumal Pramad. One is Pateksha, the other one is Anumal Pramad. Anumal means what? By intelligence, by logic. I see the sun, it is like football in size, but I use my intelligence. See, it is very far away from the earth. That is why it is looking like…”

The third source is sabda-pramana, the Vedic literatures, which are called apauruseya because their origin is beyond any human. Maharaj presents them as free from the four defects and therefore the place to bring our two inquiries.

🎙 Maharaj at 53:01 (auto-transcript): “There is a third source of knowledge. That is Shabda Praman. And they are the perfect source of knowledge. Because Shabda Praman is not by any human. They are Aporu Sheya. They are having a source which is beyond human. They are not human. That is why Shabdha Pramad is known…”

Maharaj anticipates the objection that this is a bold claim and offers his reasoning: he says no one has yet shown a single Vedic statement to be wrong, whether or not they choose to accept it.

🎙 Maharaj at 53:37 (auto-transcript): “They give you the perfect answers. Why? Because in the Vedic literatures, you don't have these four defects. You may say, how can you say that? You are so bold and rude to say that thing. Apart from the Veda, you do not get any perfect knowledge anywhere. Yes, there is proof…”

At a college programme one envious boy hands the Gita back and demands one statement in it that is right. Maharaj opens the second chapter and reads that for one who is born death is certain (Bg 2.27), then asks the boy to show one that is wrong.

Maharaj is happy when people say they will not accept blindly. He only asks for the same standard the other way: many reject the Gita without ever having read it. — “But please remember blindly don't reject anything also.”

🎙 Maharaj at 55:32 (auto-transcript): “we don't accept it. People say blindly we don't accept. I am very happy. Blindly we should not accept anything. But please remember blindly don't reject anything also. Many people say No, no, we don't accept Gita. Have you read it? It is very good. Don't blindly accept…”

Maharaj gives the example that the Vedic texts call cow dung pure and use it to cleanse places of worship, though other stool is impure. He says scientists have since reported antiseptic qualities in it, and asks how this was known when there were no laboratories.

🎙 Maharaj at 56:14 (auto-transcript): “I'll start with a very important example. Cow dung in the Vedic literature have been described as the most pure thing in this world, cow dung. And the same way they say that any stool of any animal, including human, they are not specious, they are sturdy. But the cow dung is…”

Because they are the word of God, Maharaj says, the Vedas need no amendments, whereas national constitutions are amended and scientific statements change. He jokes that Planck's constant has been revised so often that people wonder whether it is a constant or a variable.

🎙 Maharaj at 57:26 (auto-transcript): “then did it? The Vedas are the word of God. That is why they are 100% perfect. There are no amendments in the Vedic literatures the different countries they have constitutions, their amendments. The science, different statements in the science, they are changing every day.…”

Maharaj says the Vedic texts contain predictions of later personalities and kings, describe the earth as a globe, and state that plants have life, long before others were credited for it. He asks us to be saragrahi, interested in the essence, the way we simply drink water without thinking of its formula.

🎙 Maharaj at 58:30 (auto-transcript): “The Vedic literature talks about predictions. It talks about the prediction of Buddha. 5000 years back, Veda is written. Buddha appeared 2005 years back. You find these predictions are there. are there. Jesus and Muhammad are predicted in the Bhavishya Quran which was written…”

children.topic: From the Vedas to the Gita
children.note:
Accepting that the Vedas hold the Absolute Truth, the next question is how to read them. Maharaj sketches how the Vedas came into writing, why they cannot be studied in full today, and how the Bhagavad-gita gives their essence in 700 verses.

🎙 Maharaj at 60:51 (auto-transcript): “Now, the question arises, okay, Vedas are the perfect source of knowledge. I accept it. The absolute truth is mentioned in Vedic literatures. How to read them? Something about Vedas. Originally, these Vedic literatures were only one. which was 5000 years back, Vyasa appeared.…”

children.topic: Vyasa puts the Vedas in writing
children.note:
Maharaj places Vyasa at the end of Dvapara-yuga, about 5,000 years ago, and outlines the cycle of four ages. Earlier, people remembered by hearing once, so the Vedas are called sruti; foreseeing the short memory of Kali-yuga, Vyasa did not compose but edited them into four Vedas with sections and chapters.

🎙 Maharaj at 61:02 (auto-transcript): “Something about Vedas. Originally, these Vedic literatures were only one. which was 5000 years back, Vyasa appeared. He knew that in the age of Kali, you all know that is Kali Yuga which is going on, Satya Treta Dwapar Kali. Kali Yuga, 5000 years, out of which 5000 years have…”

Maharaj says that only about six percent of that body of literature survives after the upheavals of history, and even that needs Vedic Sanskrit, which hardly anyone knows now. One lifetime is not enough to study it. So what to do?

🎙 Maharaj at 63:47 (auto-transcript): “But what happened is, if somebody wants to study them, you cannot study because only 6% of them are left now today. now today. 94% has been destroyed because of different invasions, the Mughals and different different circumstances which has happened in the entire land of…”

At the start of Kali-yuga the whole of the Vedic literature is condensed into one book of 700 verses. Maharaj says that one who studies the Bhagavad-gita need not study any other part of the Vedas.

🎙 Maharaj at 65:10 (auto-transcript): “That is the reason. At the beginning of the age of Kali, at the end of Dvapara, he took all the Vedic literatures, summarized the entire Vedic literatures into one book called Bhagavad Gita. 700 verses only. 4,000 lakh verses of Vedic literatures are condensed into 700 verses…”

The Vedas teach how to live in this world and how to get out of it. Maharaj says the second is the more important part.

🎙 Maharaj at 65:58 (auto-transcript): “And especially in the Vedic literatures, there are two kinds of knowledge given. One kind of knowledge is how to live in this world. Another kind of knowledge is how to get out of this world. What is the most prestigious engineering institute in Sri Lanka? Institute of…”

children.topic: The student who wants to stay
children.note:
A boy gets into the most prestigious engineering college, such as an IIT, and declares he will stay there year after year until death. That is foolish, because one enters college in order to leave it; in the same way, however comfortable our position, we came to this world to get out of it. — “the purpose of getting to the college is what?”

🎙 Maharaj at 66:12 (auto-transcript): “What is the most prestigious engineering institute in Sri Lanka? Institute of Technology of Colombo or whatever it is, maybe. In India you have this IIT, Indian Institute of Technology. Young boy gets an admission into this college. Most prestigious college. And he is so…”

children.topic: The Upanishads show the way out
children.note:
Architecture, mathematics, economics, Ayurveda and music are all found in the Vedic sections on how to live here, and Maharaj points to the great temples that engineers still study. But the knowledge of how to leave this world is in the Upanishads, and Krishna extracts their essence as the Bhagavad-gita.

🎙 Maharaj at 69:26 (auto-transcript): “It talks about material knowledge. But that is not the most important part of the way. The most important part of the way is to get out of this world. Spiritual knowledge means that knowledge which helps you to get out of this world. And that is there in the Upanishads. The…”

children.topic: The cow, the calf, the milk
children.note:
Maharaj cites the well-known verse comparing the Upanishads to a cow: Krishna is the milkman, Arjuna the calf who drinks first, and the Gita the nectar-like milk enjoyed by those of purified intelligence. Another verse says one scripture is enough for the whole world, the Gita sung by the son of Devaki.

🎙 Maharaj at 70:14 (auto-transcript): “That is fine. Shri Pala Srimkarachari says, He compares all the Upanishads with the cow. What is the essence of cow? And who milked the cow? It's Krishna. The first person to drink the milk is a calf. So Arjuna is compared to the calf. So what did Arjuna do? he drank that…”

The last topic of the evening: there is one Gita but many commentaries, so which one to study? Maharaj's answer is that the Gita is a book of devotion and can be understood and explained only by a devotee of Krishna. — “Bhagavad Gita is a book of devotion.”

🎙 Maharaj at 71:49 (auto-transcript): “Now it takes some time. How to understand Bhagavad Gita? This is the last topic for today and then we can have this transfer. Okay, I understood. Bhagavad Gita is the essence of all the Vedic creatures. If I had this book, no other book is required. I have understood it. Now…”

The buyer asks the shopkeeper for a Gita, the one Krishna spoke to Arjuna. The shopkeeper agrees, but says so many people have written commentaries on it; which one does he want? The buyer is left confused.

🎙 Maharaj at 72:07 (auto-transcript): “it. Now I went to a shop to buy a copy of Bhagavad Gita and asked the shopkeeper, I want a Gita. And he says, which Gita you want? He says, I want the Gita which Krishna told to Arjuna. Ah, that's okay. Which one you want? Now I want a Gita which Krishna spoke to Arjuna and…”

A beggar sees a great South Indian temple as a good place for business, a tired traveller as a place to rest, a civil engineer marvels that it has stood a thousand years, an architect admires stone carved like a chain. Only the devotee goes in and worships the Lord; he alone understands what the temple is.

🎙 Maharaj at 73:07 (auto-transcript): “To give you a simple example, you have a temple. Especially in South India, huge huge temples are there. Now, a beggar, he sees the temple and says, wow, nice place for my business. He is looking at the same temple and he is thinking, this is a place I can sit and get my…”

A student introducing Maharaj at a college announces that the Gita is the best book of management and that he will speak on that. He grants that its principles can make a good manager, as others call it a book of politics, Sanskrit or history, but that is the golden pen used for scratching. A 5,000-year-old newspaper would have no value; the Gita's glory is devotion.

🎙 Maharaj at 74:55 (auto-transcript): “Once I was asked to give a class to college students and the introduction was going on. Some students were introducing me. She started her introduction saying that, Friends, we all know Bhagavad Gita is the best book of management. I never knew this. Then everybody said, yes,…”

children.topic: 4.3 — Spoken to a devotee and friend
children.note: Krishna tells Arjuna that He is speaking this ancient science to him because Arjuna is His devotee and friend. Maharaj concludes that one must first become a devotee to understand the Gita.

Among the many editions, Maharaj points to Bhagavad-gita As It Is as the one through which masses of readers have reached the Gita's conclusion of surrender to Krishna (Bg 18.66). He says this is because it was written by a devotee.

🎙 Maharaj at 78:54 (auto-transcript): “Bhagavad Gita. That is why you find there are so many editions of Bhagavad Gita being published. But what is that one Bhagavad Gita, edition of Bhagavad Gita? Transformed millions of people's lives into a Bhagavad Gita as it is. No other Bhagavad Gita can claim they They have…”

Maharaj lists four qualifications for a teacher of the Gita and four for the student. Just as parents check that a professor is certified by a university, the first test of a guru is that he is a devotee of Krishna coming in a sampradaya.

🎙 Maharaj at 79:44 (auto-transcript): “That is why we should learn Bhagavad Gita from a devotee of Krishna, that is the first qualification of a Guru. That he should be a devotee of Krishna, coming under the Sampradhaya, like if you want to send your children to some college or school or something like that, then…”

Maharaj calls the sampradayas universities set up by Krishna for handing down complete knowledge of the Absolute Truth, headed by Brahma, Rudra (Lord Shiva), Sri (Lakshmi) and the four Kumaras. ISKCON may look modern with its projectors, but its founder-acarya comes in the Gaudiya line from Brahma, so the message is undistorted and keeps its effect.

🎙 Maharaj at 80:11 (auto-transcript): “What is that university which teaches Bhagavad Gita? Krishna has set up four universities. They are known as Sampradayas. Samyak Rupena Pradaya. Prakrishna Rupena Daya. Sam means absolute truth. Pra means Prakrishna Rupena, complete. Daya means to give. The system by which…”

nodeData.topic: Day 02 · The Science of the Soul
nodeData.note: Bg 2.13, 2.20, 15.1, 3.4, 3.9 · a class by HH Bhakti Padma Saurabha Pracharaka Swami. After recapping day one, Maharaj takes up the jiva: five proofs that the soul exists (common sense, the logic of 'my body', consciousness, out-of-body and near-death reports, past-life memories), the ten components of our existence from gross body to Supersoul, what travels at death, and the soul's nature as eternal, conscious and blissful. He argues that the real problem of life is passing our years without this knowledge, using the musk deer, the lost keys and the man who mourns his watch. A long question session covers the benefit of spiritual life, whether life is really suffering, the reality of the spiritual world, other religions, and how duty offered to Krishna becomes spiritual. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note:
Maharaj welcomes everyone to the second day and asks why they came when their friends did not: because they have inquisitiveness, the quality that makes one a human being. He recalls the first aphorism of the Vedanta-sutra and notes that we try to eat, sleep, mate and defend in a sophisticated way, yet past thirty-five our diet is restricted and on the best bed anxiety keeps us awake. — “Why you are here? Why your friend is not here?”

🎙 Maharaj at 00:02 (auto-transcript): “Let's welcome you all to the second day of our course. Yesterday we discussed about the introduction to Bhagavad Gita. While discussing about the introduction to Bhagavad Gita, the first point we discussed was that why are we here? Why you are here? Why your friend is not…”

The first enquiry is the goal of life: the human body is a vehicle, and a car is useless if the driver has no destination. The second is the cause of suffering: chasing enjoyment without it is like trying medicines from the chemist's shelf without a diagnosis, which only aggravates the disease. — “We are not just supposed to live our life.”

🎙 Maharaj at 02:20 (auto-transcript): “And one of the two prime enquiries in life, that is what we discussed yesterday. The first enquiry in our life should be that, what is the goal of life? What is the purpose of life? If we don't know the purpose of life, what is the use of our living? Like if you are driving a…”

Of the three sources of knowledge, sense perception is flawed because we make mistakes, fall into illusion (a spoon in a glass of water looks bent), cheat and are cheated (Maharaj points to advertising), and have limited senses that hear only between 20 and 20,000 hertz. Science rests on the senses, he says, and its constant talk of progress shows it is incomplete; so we inquire from the Vedas, and he recalls yesterday's examples of their authority.

🎙 Maharaj at 05:11 (auto-transcript): “raised yesterday was where we should inquire from we should inquire from the Vedic literatures ask why because the Vedas are the perfect source of knowledge yesterday we discussed about three Brahmanas three sources of knowledge the Pratiksha Pramana, Inferenship, Anumana…”

Maharaj says only a small part of the Vedas remains and even that is too much for many lifetimes, so Krishna condensed it into the Bhagavad-gita. The Vedas teach how to live in this world and how to get out of it, and the second matters more: an intelligent student in the best college always thinks of how to pass out of it, while only a fool wants to stay year after year.

children.topic: Who can teach, who can learn
children.note: The Gita is studied under a teacher who is a devotee of Krishna in a sampradaya, learned, self-controlled and teaching by example; Maharaj recalls Krishna telling Arjuna that he receives this science because he is His devotee and friend. The student is inquisitive, humble and ready to serve. Of the Gita's five subjects, today's is the jiva.

Today's subject is the jiva, the living entity or soul. Before describing it Maharaj sets out to prove that it exists, beginning with common sense and then logic.

We say 'I know this', but do we know who that 'I' is? Are the eyes seeing, is the mind seeing, who is hearing right now? children.topic: The brain is not the mind
children.note:
When someone behaves strangely the neurologist finds the brain perfectly fine and sends him to another department, the psychiatrist. The mind cannot be weighed or measured by gross means. 'Prabhuji, you spoke of body and mind, now tell us about the soul itself.' Maharaj gives three qualities: sat, eternal; cit, conscious, the reason we can feel pleasure, pain and every emotion; and ananda, blissful.

🎙 Maharaj at 58:12 (auto-transcript): “Oh Prabhuji, you are talking so much about that and this. But tell me about what exactly is the soul? You spoke about body, the mind and so many things. I want to know about the soul. Now we will talk about the soul. The qualities of the soul. The first and foremost quality…”

Maharaj recites the verse and goes through it word by word: it teaches that birth and death belong to the body only and never touch the soul. So we neither truly celebrate a birth nor need lament 'he died'.

The body only seems alive because the soul is present, yet we care for it alone and forget the soul. Children spend lakhs to keep a father in the ICU, but the moment the doctor says he is gone the same body is burned. For whom was the money spent? — “the body is always dead.”

🎙 Maharaj at 59:27 (auto-transcript): “Actually what to speak of saying body died, the body is always dead. The body is always dead. It is just because the presence of soul in the body, the body seems to be alive. It seems to be alive, but it is our foolishness. What we do? We just take care of the body. We just…”

Ananda is the soul's nature. If so, why am I suffering? Because that nature is forgotten, and we look for happiness on the material platform, in this restaurant, that channel, that place, this person, instead of the spiritual one.

🎙 Maharaj at 62:17 (auto-transcript): “What is the third quality of the soul? The third quality of the soul is, it is Anandamaya. You must have heard this term, Satchitananda. What is Satchitananda? Sat comes from the word Sanatana, Chin comes from the word Chaitanya, Chinmaya and Ananda means what? Bliss. The…”

The musk deer smells a wonderful fragrance and runs to find its source. The faster it runs the stronger the scent, so it keeps running until one day it drops dead. Maharaj says this is our story. — “This foolish deer doesn't know it is coming from its own body.”

🎙 Maharaj at 62:56 (auto-transcript): “There is an example given, Kasturi Brugab. There is a musk deer. From its body, wonderful fragrance comes out of its body, this deer. And this deer is thinking, where is this fragrance coming from? He thinks, ah, it is coming from here, let me go. It starts going towards this…”

A man misses his keys late at night and searches only under the street lamp, just because there is light there, though they could have fallen anywhere. We too look for happiness only where our senses can see, and never consider the spiritual platform.

🎙 Maharaj at 65:03 (auto-transcript): “you are coming from your office to your home it is late night it so happens you put your hand in the pocket keys are lost then you go back to your office searching you drove your car where you are searching exactly at the place where the street lane is there just because…”

Thirty, forty, fifty years have passed and we still have not understood 'I am not this body, I am spirit soul' or learned the Bhagavad-gita. Maharaj calls this the real problem; because it goes unrecognised we carry a long list of others.

🎙 Maharaj at 65:59 (auto-transcript): “we are all facing and instead of concentrating on the real problem that is self-realization we are concentrating on what so many different problems actually the real problem is we are already 30 40 50 years 50 60 is going to come till now we have not understood that i have…”

A man of small salary saves for fifteen years to buy a Mercedes, and on the drive home a truck smashes it. He screams about the police station while the driver begs him to come to hospital and look at his arm: the forearm is gone. He grows angrier still, because his golden watch went with it. We too cry for the watch while life itself passes without self-realization.

🎙 Maharaj at 66:49 (auto-transcript): “there was one person who wanted to buy a mercedes and he was not very rich he used to earn few thousand rupees a month and somehow for 15 years he worked hard and saved every penny so that one One day he had enough bank balance to go and do the down payment and get the car.…”

Since we are spirit, only spiritual things can satisfy us. If matter could, those with the best material facilities would be happy; Maharaj asks why so many of them turn to drugs and frustration instead. — “It can never satisfy anyone because we are not matter. We are spiritual beings.”

🎙 Maharaj at 69:13 (auto-transcript): “because you are not this body, you are spirit soul since you are soul only spiritual things can satisfy you the soul is spiritual and you are spiritual you are soul, the soul is spiritual only spiritual things can satisfy us we are not this body, bodies matter nothing…”

A child is crying because his team lost the cricket match. The mother reminds him of tomorrow's exam and he stops at once and opens his book: seeing a higher problem dissolves the lower ones. Complaints like 'she did not welcome me properly' fade when we see that every passing second brings death nearer.

🎙 Maharaj at 70:46 (auto-transcript): “Like a child is crying. Mother comes and asks, what is the problem? The child says, India lost the cricket match or Sri Lanka lost the cricket match. I have to say Sri Lanka lost the cricket match, I suppose. Now, what is your exam? The child immediately opens the book and…”

This is why the first thing Krishna teaches, from verse 11 to verse 30 of the second chapter, is the soul. Maharaj says austerity, sacrifice and charity without this knowledge remain ritual and religiosity, and he reads Krishna's closing call to give up all dharmas as an invitation to be spiritual, not merely religious.

🎙 Maharaj at 72:13 (auto-transcript): “So this is the knowledge of the soul that is going to give us the real benefit of life. That is why Krishna, when he spoke the Bhagavad Gita, the first thing what he gave was the knowledge of the soul. The second chapter starting from the 11th verse to the 30th verse, he just…”

'I am not this body, I am spirit soul' answers racial problems, since the soul is neither black nor white, and economic ones, since greed comes from securing the body. He corrects the phrase 'my soul will leave': I, the soul, will leave. And nothing material carries over: last life's crore in the bank cannot be withdrawn, and last life's PhD starts again at ABCD.

🎙 Maharaj at 74:01 (auto-transcript): “Now we say, what is the benefit which the world is going to have? You name a problem in this world. Maharaj stops and repeats that the most important part of the course is not what he speaks but what the audience asks.

children.topic: Q1 · What's in it for me?
children.note:
A listener asks why he should care for the soul now if he will not remember it next life. Maharaj gives two benefits: the immediate one, which he calls klesaghni, relief from being affected by misery; and the ultimate one, that a perfected soul does not take birth again but returns to the spiritual world, with no more school and scoldings.

🎙 Question from the floor at 76:24 (auto-transcript): “You used asking, what's in it for me, right? Yes. You're saying, okay, I'm not going to enjoy the next life. I won't have the consciousness to enjoy the next life. Why should I take care of my soul this life? Okay. How do I get the benefit of my soul this life in the next…”

Difficulties will still come, and anyone who promises a blessing that removes all problems is fooling you. But as rain does not wet one who has cover, the practitioner is not affected. A newcomer cannot yet perceive the next-life benefit, but this one can be felt at once.

🎙 Maharaj at 77:04 (auto-transcript): “First thing is, as soon as you take up the process of self-realization, The first benefit is Kaleshavni. You will not be affected by the miseries of this world. It is not the miseries or the difficulties are not going to come. They are going to come. If somebody says, oh,…”

Duryodhana sits in a palace with servants and soldiers; the Pandavas are in the forest among wild animals with no one to protect them. Yet they sleep peacefully while he lies awake through the years of their exile, worrying about their return. They have Krishna with them.

🎙 Maharaj at 79:05 (auto-transcript): “to give you a small example Duryodhana was in the palace so many servants so many soldiers to protect him he was very powerful, he was a king Pandavas were in the forest there had nobody to protect them All the Pandavas at night, they were sleeping peacefully in spite of all…”

A listener objects that life has happy moments too, so why call it miserable and look for an exit? Maharaj agrees suffering is not constant: happiness and suffering alternate, each sandwiched between two of the other.

🎙 Question from the floor at 80:32 (auto-transcript): “we all live a happy life also. Of course we have sufferings. There are happy moments also. Why do we consider that this life is full of suffering, unbearable, therefore we need find an exit and and one more question is that is a spiritual world that we are talking about after…”

Nice butter between two burnt slices, or good bread with butter gone bitter: either way the sandwich is spoiled. In India he uses kheer, sweet rice with milk, sugar and dry fruits, and just one spoon of sand in it.

🎙 Maharaj at 81:31 (auto-transcript): “afraid is of happiness and of happiness, the afraid is of suffering. children.topic: We talk only of the fever
children.note:
After a perfect week's holiday, if you or your son come home with a fever, that is all you speak about. The reason is that the soul's nature is unbroken enjoyment, so 'a little happiness, a little misery' never satisfies it, and we aim for eternal life in the spiritual world.

🎙 Maharaj at 83:28 (auto-transcript): “suffering is there in spite of a nice wonderful holiday you have wonderful one week holiday everything went according to your plan you enjoyed a lot it is when came back to your house you caught up with a disease which will be more concerned for you what will you talk about…”

children.topic: Q3 · Is the spiritual world hypothetical?
children.note:
The same listener finds a spiritual world after death hypothetical. Maharaj answers with an argument from physics, a philosophical one, a Gita verse, and our own search for happiness.

🎙 Question from the floor at 84:48 (auto-transcript): “of enjoyment in the spiritual world. Now your next question is, is there something spiritual world? It is very hypothetical. First thing is I have taught something which the modern science also accepts. Those of you who have studied some physics at higher level, there's so…”

Maharaj traces physics from Dalton's indivisible atom through Rutherford to more and more particles and finally antimatter. He reasons that if every particle needs its opposite, the material world as a whole should have an opposite too, which he identifies as spiritual.

🎙 Maharaj at 85:03 (auto-transcript): “accepts. Those of you who have studied some physics at higher level, there's so much of research was done in many many years to find out what is atom, what are the components within the atom. First, Dalton told atom is the smallest indivisible substance. And then he told,…”

The chairs in this room did not arrange themselves; a conscious person moved them. So the whole material world has someone behind it and something it rests on, as the famous saying goes, 'give me a fixed point and I will lift the earth'. An eternal soul needs an eternal home, where life is the opposite of the temporary, ignorant, joyless life here.

🎙 Maharaj at 86:35 (auto-transcript): “Now, the philosophical argument behind this is, this is material world. Everywhere there is matter. Do you think it just came by chance? It has been created. Where from it has been created? Any movement of matter which happens in this world, it is because there is a spirit…”

Krishna describes the material world as a tree with roots up and branches down. Maharaj notes that we see such a tree only as a reflection on the bank of a river or lake, so somewhere there is an original tree where everything stands the right way up.

children.topic: We search for what we lost
children.note:
Everyone searches for happiness, and one searches only for what one once had and has lost. Nobody wants to die, so we must have known deathlessness, and it is not found anywhere here. Spiritualists are not against enjoyment, Maharaj adds: it is the soul's nature; the mistake is looking in the wrong place.

🎙 Maharaj at 89:11 (auto-transcript): “the real tree, where everything is found in its proper perspective. Last point, everybody this world is searching for what? Happiness. But they are not finding it. Even they find it, it is mixed with misery. Why they are searching, tell me. Why they are searching for…”

Maharaj says the full answer comes on day four with the three modes of nature. Everyone is born with a nature, seated subtly in the false ego and spreading through mind, intelligence and body, and is forced to act by it; but by higher association, like the friend who brought you to this Gita class, one can gradually go beyond it.

🎙 Question from the floor at 91:50 (auto-transcript): “Sour as a person. Which is controlling us the most? children.topic: Q5 · How to maintain Krishna consciousness?
children.note:
We maintain a family or a business by giving it attention, so first be concerned about your Krishna consciousness. Then keep the company of someone already Krishna conscious: something will always push you away, and you need a friend who calls about the program just when you were planning a movie. The last day will cover practice. — “Without association, you cannot maintain Krishna Consciousness.”

So you're asking how to maintain. How do you maintain your family? How do you maintain your business? You maintain your family, you…”

A listener asks whether traditions such as Christianity converge on the soul, since Indians are more exposed to the idea. Maharaj replies that the knowledge is not Indian property; whether one accepts it depends on the individual, not on country or religion.

🎙 Question from the floor at 96:04 (auto-transcript): “It pertains to, let's say, the existence of soul. There are several other religions, let's say Christianity. Is there any convergence of thoughts? It is not that everybody in India believes it. At least we are exposed more. See, this word India was given by the British.”

'India' and 'Hindustan' are recent names given by others, Maharaj says; the scriptures speak of Bharata-varsha, ruled by King Bharata and far larger than today's country. He holds that Vedic culture was once spread worldwide and that Veda simply means knowledge, with nothing sectarian in it.

🎙 Maharaj at 96:48 (auto-transcript): “See, this word India was given by the British. This word India was not there a few hundred years back. Even the word Hindustan was given with the Muslims. It is actually Bharata. This Bharata Varsha, this Bharata Khanda as described in the Vedic literature, the entire earth…”

Srila Prabhupada presented the soul in the West as a science and those interested took it up. Maharaj finds it harder with pious Indians, who quote a line of the Gita and start teaching him. No schoolchild rejects Newton or Edison for his country or faith; and Krishna's statement that death is certain for one who is born is neither Hindu nor Muslim, just true. — “Mathematics is the same for everyone.”

Citing the hierarchy of needs, a listener asks whether there is a stage of life for taking this up. Maharaj says the same question came up that morning in a devotee's home: people assume spirituality means renunciation and that they must choose between family duty and being spiritual.

🎙 Question from the floor at 102:13 (auto-transcript): “There is a hierarchy of needs. Maharaj recites Krishna's statement in the third chapter that merely taking sannyasa does not bring perfection, and asks why people still equate spirituality with giving things up.

children.topic: Duty keeps the senses in check
children.note:
Sacrifice means doing something even when I do not feel like it, and that purifies. Going to a job we do not enjoy is such a sacrifice. Imagine one week with no responsibilities and the family away: Maharaj says we would only watch television or worse.

🎙 Maharaj at 104:35 (auto-transcript): “In the entire Bhagavad Gita, Krishna talks about sacrifice. Sacrifice means I do something even if I don't want to. That is called sacrifice. And by doing that, we become purified. That keeps us self-controlled. That keeps our senses under control. Like for example, you don't…”

Work becomes spiritual when it is done for Krishna. Market flowers offered in the temple become sacred though they are still matter, and iron kept in fire takes on the qualities of fire; in the same way duties connected with the Lord purify us. — “there is no contradiction between spirituality and responsibilities.”

Milk boiled down into peda and eaten by the kilo upsets the stomach; the same milk made into curd is the cure. Responsibility without Krishna consciousness becomes frustration, and with it becomes the remedy. Arjuna's mistake was to think he could be spiritual by dropping his duty; Krishna tells him to fight while remembering Him. Maharaj invites everyone to the weekly Gita classes.

nodeData.note: Bg 2.20, 7.7, 13.23, 14.27, 15.15, 18.63 · a class by HH Bhakti Padma Saurabha Pracharaka Swami. After recapping the science of the soul, Maharaj turns to God: he shows how shaky mere belief is, traces atheism from the dawn of creation to its modern scientific dress, and argues from order, design, control, energy and creation that there must be a Creator. He then explains why one God is taught through different religions, why the only real reason to accept God is love, and how Brahman, Paramatma and Bhagavan are three views of the same Lord, like sunshine, reflection and the sun. The class ends with questions on how to love God and why the Supersoul lets people do wrong. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note:

children.topic: Faith shifts from church to science
children.note:
Maharaj recounts that people were once pious churchgoers. Then Newton, sitting under a tree, asked why the apple fell down and not up, and classical mechanics began. nodeData.topic: Day 04 · Who Is God? Bhagavan Krishna
nodeData.note: SB 1.3.28, SB 2.3.10, SB 4.31.14, Brahma-samhita 5.44, 5.50, 5.52 · a class by HH Bhakti Padma Saurabha Pracharaka Swami. Maharaj defines Bhagavan as the person who holds six opulences in full, shows that such a being must be a person full of emotions and all-attractive, and so arrives at the name Krishna. He then explains how Durga, Ganesha, Lord Shiva, Brahma and Surya are Krishna's devotees and administrators, and concludes that worship is for Krishna and respect is for the devatas, like watering the root of a tree. A long question-and-answer session covers Shiva worship, Tirupati Balaji, why God is called 'He', and Krishna as the source of all incarnations. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

Maharaj lifts his kartals: he has a form, but the energy that lifted them has none, just as a generator has form and its electricity does not. Scriptures that say God is formless speak of Brahman, His energy; those that describe His form speak of Bhagavan, the energetic, whose form is not material. — “but the sunshine doesn't have form”

Brahman and Paramatma are partial understandings; the highest is Bhagavan. Maharaj explains the word: bhaga means opulence or quality, and Bhagavan is the one who possesses all of them completely.

🎙 Maharaj at 11:25 (auto-transcript): “is when you understand Bhagavan. Now let us understand this term Bhagavan. It is a very simple word. Bhagavan. Bhag means bhagya. We say that bhagyavan. It is Bhagavan. One who has got all the bhaga. Bhaga means opulences. Bhaga means qualities. So there are six qualities…”

Citing Parasara, Maharaj lists them: all riches, all beauty, all knowledge, all strength, all fame and all renunciation. The test for each is that nobody is equal to Him and nobody is greater.

🎙 Maharaj at 11:47 (auto-transcript): “which are present in Bhagawan in full. What are the six qualities? Nobody should be as rich as him and nobody should be more…”

We too have these qualities, but only a little and only for a while. Maharaj points to last year's Miss Universe crowning this year's: one year and the title is gone; and one person has beauty without riches, another riches without knowledge.

🎙 Maharaj at 13:29 (auto-transcript): “but we find in this world we also have these six qualities but we cannot claim I am all beautiful even if you claim that I am all beautiful okay you claim I am the most beautifulest person Miss Universe you may say okay but the next year the Miss Universe of the previous year…”

Maharaj tells of a famous beauty proposing to the elderly author Bernard Shaw so that their child would have his intelligence and her looks. Shaw replies that he is afraid of the reverse. We want the best of both worlds, but only Bhagavan has everything. — “very wonderful but only afraid if the reverse happens”

🎙 Maharaj at 14:20 (auto-transcript): “like once it so happened that there was a beauty queen at once for a time her name was Morgan Munro most of you must be knowing her and at the time same time there was one very intelligent person who was a great author Bernard Shaw So both were well known around the world One…”

With a little money or beauty we become proud and want to show off. Maharaj calls it Bhagavan's speciality that He has every opulence in full and is still completely renounced.

🎙 Maharaj at 15:42 (auto-transcript): “You may have one as one thing, you may don't have another thing, but Bhagawan is one who has everything. He possesses everything including renunciation. This is one very special quality, in spite of Bhagawan being all rich, he is all renounced. In spite of Bhagawan being all…”

Qualities imply a personality, and a personality implies a person. Since Bhagavan by definition has six qualities in full, Maharaj concludes He is a person as much as you and I are, not an impersonal light. — “As much as you are a person, I am a person, Bhagawan is a person.”

🎙 Maharaj at 16:40 (auto-transcript): “Now, let us see. This quality, what does this qualities imply? Whoever has these qualities, qualities imply that there is a personality. And personality implies a person. Actually a person is recognized through his personality. And a personality is made up of qualities. How…”

How do we tell two people apart? By their different sets of qualities. Maharaj reasons that the more the qualities develop, the fuller the personality, so the one with all qualities is the fullest person.

🎙 Maharaj at 16:50 (auto-transcript): “Whoever has these qualities, qualities imply that there is a personality. And personality implies a person. Actually a person is recognized through his personality. And a personality is made up of qualities. How you distinguish between two people, two persons? Because two…”

While chanting in the temple Maharaj greets a family who have driven about 50 km for darshan. The moment the elderly gentleman stands before the Deities he closes his eyes; Maharaj sees in this the impersonal idea of God.

🎙 Maharaj at 18:39 (auto-transcript): “So, God is one who is full of emotions. Like sometimes you find people who come in front of God and then close their eyes. Just imagine, once it so happened that I was there in the temple, chanting my mantras. I was just walking in the temple and chanting Madhantras. At the…”

children.topic: A friend who shuts his eyes
children.note:
Imagine a friend flies in to see you, you open the door, and he closes his eyes and says he is meditating on you. Maharaj asks how awkward that would feel: a person in front of us is meant to be seen and spoken with.

🎙 Maharaj at 20:06 (auto-transcript): “the Supreme Lord just imagine your friend comes many kilometres flying and he came to meet you he knocks the door you open the door and then as soon as you open the door, he closes his eyes. How awkward you feel, isn't it? Why, why he's closing his eyes? If you know you're…”

As a boy in the railway colony in Mysore, Maharaj and his friends stone the mango tree at the biggest officer's house and run with the fruit, though mangoes are rotting at home. He asks where that special pleasure comes from: every emotion we feel exists originally and perfectly in God, and ours is a perverted reflection. — “where is this emotion coming from”

🎙 Maharaj at 21:18 (auto-transcript): “To give you a small example, I still remember, in my childhood I used to stay in in the Railway colony in Mysore. children.topic: He likes to play and dance
children.note:
We like to play, sing and dance only because that liking is first present in Bhagavan in perfection. Maharaj notes the scriptures describe Him as the very form of all rasas.

🎙 Maharaj at 23:15 (auto-transcript): “to play. Why? God doesn't like to play or what? The very fact that we have a liking to play it is because God has a liking to play. Like we like to sing and dance, isn't it? Now why we like to sing and dance? Because the liking of singing and dancing was originally present in…”

What do qualities do? They attract. Since Bhagavan has every quality in full He must be all-attractive, and Maharaj asks the audience for the one Sanskrit word that means all-attractive.

🎙 Maharaj at 23:53 (auto-transcript): “Now, let us discuss one more point about the qualities. What do we do with these qualities? With these qualities, what do we do? We attract. Whoever has these qualities more, they become more attractive. If somebody is more rich, they become more attractive. Somebody is more…”

The rich, the beautiful like film stars, the learned and even the renounced draw people to them. We attract to the extent we have a quality, so the one who has all of them completely attracts everyone.

🎙 Maharaj at 24:26 (auto-transcript): “So actually every quality in itself has an attractive feature in it. The more we possess these qualities, the more attractive we become. That is why to the extent we have these qualities, to that extent we become attractive. Now Bhagawan has been defined as what? As one who…”

From the root krish come the Hindi akarshan and, Maharaj suggests, even the similar-sounding English word attraction. Krishna means all-attractive, Bhagavan is all-attractive, so Bhagavan is Krishna: simple logic. — “A equal to B, B equal to C and A equal to C”

🎙 Maharaj at 25:37 (auto-transcript): “Now, what is that one word in Sanskrit which means all-attractive? Bhagawan is all-attractive. And what is that one word in Sanskrit which means all-attractive? Karashayati, krishbuachara shabdaha. Karashayati means, if you see, the English word is also having a similar…”
Maharaj quotes the Bhagavatam's phrase 'krsnas tu bhagavan svayam' to show that the word Bhagavan belongs in its full sense to Krishna alone.

People may say each group calls its own favourite Bhagavan, so why believe anyone, even him? Maharaj points to the Gita: whenever Krishna speaks it is written 'Sri Bhagavan uvaca', and Brahma says in the Brahma-samhita that Krishna is the supreme controller. Being supreme does not make Him impersonal; He is the supreme person.

🎙 Maharaj at 27:24 (auto-transcript): “People may say, oh you people are from Wisconsin, that is why you say Krishna is Bhagavan. If you go to some other satsang, they say somebody is Bhagavan. If you go to some other place, they say Bhagavan. But why do you believe somebody? And why do you believe me also? Let us…”

When Krishna appears and performs His pastimes He shows by His acts that He is Bhagavan, manifesting each of the six opulences.

🎙 Maharaj at 28:45 (auto-transcript): “Now, let us see, when Krishna appeared, when he did pastimes, he showed that he is Bhagawan. How he showed? He manifested all the opulences, the six qualities. The first quality as we discussed is Aishwarya riches. In Dwaraka, Krishna had 16,108 wives. We know one itself is…”

In Dwaraka Krishna has 16,108 queens, a palace for each, and all are fully satisfied; Maharaj has the audience imagine the saris alone. For beauty, the gopis scold Brahma for creating eyelids, since each blink costs them a moment of seeing Krishna, whose beauty surpasses millions of Cupids.

🎙 Maharaj at 28:59 (auto-transcript): “The first quality as we discussed is Aishwarya riches. In Dwaraka, Krishna had 16,108 wives. We know one itself is so difficult. And for each wife, he had a palace. And all the servants and all the wives were completely satisfied. And they used to wear 10 saris a day, cherry…”

People do all sorts of things to be noticed, yet Krishna's simple childhood act of stealing butter 5,000 years ago is still talked about without any advertisement. Devotees speak of Him, and those who deny Him also speak of Him. — “The most famous person in the entire existence”

🎙 Maharaj at 30:23 (auto-transcript): “Fame Just see people, what all people do To become famous, isn't it They try to somehow get attention on people. For that they do all kinds of things. But Krishna, simple activity, childish activity, stealing butter. What did he do? 5000 years back. Still we talk about it. It…”

As a seven-year-old boy Krishna playfully holds Govardhan on His little finger for seven days and nights. Maharaj contrasts this with weightlifters who strain, hold for seconds and drop; Krishna's body stays as soft as butter.

🎙 Maharaj at 31:34 (auto-transcript): “I don't know when he talks about whom. It is him only now. So that he is the most famous person, the most strength, seven-year-old boy, Krishna. He lifted Gordhan for seven days and seven nights with a little finger. And how did he lift it? Playfully lifted it. Not like our…”

As Lord Ramachandra, about to be crowned, He goes to the forest for fourteen years just so His father's word is kept, with the same smile on His face. We lose a few hundred rupees and cannot stop thinking about it.

🎙 Maharaj at 32:35 (auto-transcript): “So, Krishna is a strength. And in spite of all these things, he is so renounced. When he appeared in Lord Ramachandra, just, his father did not even order him. It was just, if he doesn't go to forest, his father's world cannot be kept. That's all. He was just to be crowned as…”

Most books are forgotten in months or a few years, but the Bhagavad-gita has guided millions for 5,000 years. Maharaj adds Krishna's own statement that He knows the past, present and future of every living being. — “Can there be any better book of knowledge than this?”

Maharaj says that an Indian audience enjoys the course until this point and then objects: all should be seen equally. He answers that everyone already knows there is one Bhagavan and many devatas, counted as 33 crores, who are subservient to Him, and since it is Navaratri he begins with Durga.

🎙 Maharaj at 34:51 (auto-transcript): “Especially when you speak this particular subject of establishing Krishna, Supreme Lord Bhagawan, especially when you speak it in front of the Indian audience, they always think, Prabhuji, till yesterday the course was very nice, but this I cannot accept. So many people,…”
The Brahma-samhita verse Maharaj recites describes Durga as the shadow energy of Krishna who carries out creation, maintenance and destruction of this world in line with His will.

Maharaj points to the well-known form of Durga in the Himalayas called Vaishnavi. The name itself, he says, tells us she is a devotee of Vishnu and not an independent goddess; Krishna has entrusted her with the care of the whole material world.

🎙 Maharaj at 38:44 (auto-transcript): “You have nava durga, nava lakshmi, so many things. But, there is one special form of durga. You must be knowing about it. A mother nourishes her child and also disciplines him, so the one we call Ma also carries a trishul. Maharaj explains its three points as the three miseries: from our own body and mind, from other living beings such as mosquitoes and people, and from nature, such as tsunamis and earthquakes. — “at the same time she has a Trishul.”

🎙 Maharaj at 39:39 (auto-transcript): “She is such a qualified person that Krishna has appointed her to take care of the entire material world. Entire material world is taken care of by her like a mother. What does the mother do? Mother takes care of the child very nicely. She nourishes the child. Whatever the…”

After the Bhuj earthquake devotees go with doctors, cooks and kirtan, because food and medicine cannot heal grief. In a flattened village an old man asks why Mother Durga, whom they all worship, became so harsh; the speaker replies that when children ignore the father's words the mother does not stay silent. Maharaj applies it to not hearing Krishna's Gita. — “No medicines can cure their emotional depression.”

🎙 Maharaj at 41:10 (auto-transcript): “So these Tishula, the three points indicate these three kinds of miseries. She is giving miseries. You may say, why Durga is giving miseries to me? Dur means difficult and gama means to go: a durga is a fort or jail that is hard to get out of. The material world is such a place and Durga is its superintendent, who, like any jail superintendent, really wants the inmates to behave well and be released early.

Maharaj tells a story of Tihar jail under the officer Kiran Bedi being run so well that released prisoners came back asking to be let in again. Trying to make the jail comfortable is foolish; Durga wants us to leave this world by taking shelter of Krishna. — “Though you make this jail comfortable, but you are not free.”

Maharaj turns to Ganesha, usually the first to be spoken of. He is Vighnesha, the remover of obstacles for those who seek progress in the three worlds, and his form with a human body and an elephant's head is unique.

The Brahma-samhita verse Maharaj recites says that Ganesha gets his power to remove obstacles by holding the feet of Govinda on his head.

Parvati forms a powerful boy from sandal paste and posts him at the door while she bathes. He refuses to let even Lord Shiva in, turns down a boon and demands a fight, until Shiva in anger throws his trishul and the boy's head is cut off; Parvati weeps.

Shiva's attendants are sent north to bring the head of the first being they find. Maharaj says it is not an ordinary elephant but one of the Vinayakas, beings with human bodies and elephant heads, and that Ganesha is delighted because the head resembles a form of Vishvaksena in Vaikuntha.

The devatas send Ganesha to write down the Mahabharata for Vyasa. Ganesha's condition is that Vyasa must dictate without a pause; Vyasa's is that Ganesha must understand each verse before writing it. Maharaj says that, eager to write about Krishna, Ganesha breaks off his own tusk to write with, near Badri.

Arriving in Sri Lanka, Maharaj hears much about Lord Shiva. He presents him as the greatest of Vaishnavas, always chanting on his beads, which is why a Shiva temple is found wherever there is a Vishnu temple.

Lord Shiva daily chants the Vishnu-sahasranama. Parvati asks for something short and simple, and he tells her that the name of Rama equals the thousand names of Vishnu. Maharaj asks what more proof is needed that Shiva wants everyone to chant the Lord's name.

Maharaj says Brahma describes himself in the Brahma-samhita as a jewel that shines with light received from elsewhere: Krishna is the real creator. Brahma is a devotee and the first guru of the Brahma-Madhva-Gaudiya line, not an independent God.

A tailor makes the shirt, but only from cloth the weaver made first. Vishnu supplies the ingredients of creation and Brahma, like a mason, builds with them, so he is the secondary creator.

children.topic: Surya turns the wheel of time
children.note: From the Brahma-samhita Maharaj explains that the sun is the eye of the Lord and moves on its path by His order. Each sunrise and sunset takes away one day of our life. Krishna also tells Arjuna that He first spoke the Gita to the sun-god, who is thus His disciple.

These five and all the other devatas help Krishna administer the world, like the many ministers who run departments under a Prime Minister.

Maharaj raises the question on everyone's mind: I have worshipped the devatas for so many years, so how should I relate to them now? His answer is that Krishna takes the central place and the devatas a respected lower place, and they are happy with that.

🎙 Maharaj at 68:57 (auto-transcript): “ask a question how should we relate to the demigods what we should do to them I have been worshipping them for so many years what we should do now comes a very important point worship should be only to Krishna and others should be respected that is why the Vishnu Quran says…”

Citing scripture, Maharaj says worship is meant for Vishnu alone, yet the devatas must never be disrespected, because they are advanced devotees appointed by Krishna. Ganesha is pleased when we read the Gita and Lord Shiva when we chant Krishna's names.

People with material desires line up before Lord Shiva, who is Ashutosh, easily pleased; even Ravana got boons. This verse advises that whether a person is full of desires, free of desires or wanting liberation, he should worship the Supreme Person with intense devotion.

children.topic: Q2 · Vows and donations at Tirupati?
children.note:

children.topic: Q3 · Three questions from one guest
children.note:
One guest asks three things together: why God is spoken of as male, how the Gita's date of 5,000 years fits with Vyasa's writing, and whether God is a supreme energy. Maharaj takes them one by one.

🎙 Question from the floor at 90:01 (auto-transcript): “How did this about six qualities present? Male orientation means? Male orientation. There were a couple of references where we spoke of Krishna being 5000 years before. Yes. The day one when we understood, we asked him actually in the scriptures and from there the condensed…”

The soul is neither male nor female; all matter and all souls are prakriti, the energy, and Krishna alone is purusha, the energetic and the enjoyer. Our trouble begins when we think we are the enjoyer. Maharaj cites the sages of Dandakaranya who, though in male bodies, wished to marry Lord Rama. — “There is only one Purusha. It is Krishna.”

🎙 Maharaj at 91:14 (auto-transcript): “See, when you think of male, generally we have an idea of some male and female in this world. But actually, whatever you see in this world, whether it is male or female, whether it is neuter, gender like this, all are female. They are all prakriti. We have, we think, I am a…”

Maharaj explains that the Mahabharata is among Vyasa's later works, before the Vedanta-sutra and the Bhagavatam, and was recorded as Vaishampayana narrated it to Janamejaya of Pariksit's line. So '5,000 years' is a broad span, not an exact date.

🎙 Maharaj at 93:52 (auto-transcript): “Now, your second question is about the chronology of Bhagavad Gita. How Vyasa wrote it? I just used the word 5000 years back. What happened is Vyasa, Mahabharata was the later writings of Vyasa. The last work of Vyasa was Srimad. And before that he had written the Vedanta…”

Seeing God only as a supreme power is a limited understanding. Behind every energy is its possessor, and Krishna is the person who possesses the supreme energy. — “But we discussed, energy is never independent.”

🎙 Maharaj at 95:39 (auto-transcript): “As I have told in today's class, some people have some idea that God is some power, some energy. Isn't it? Supreme Lord. Yeah, supreme power, supreme energy. But we discussed, energy is never independent. Energy behind every energy is energetic. So, to see God as our supreme…”

children.topic: Q4 · Is Krishna an incarnation of Vishnu?
children.note:
Maharaj says he left this topic for questions on purpose. The common idea is that one Vishnu comes down ten times, but there are three Vishnus for creation, and the word Vishnu, 'all-pervading', applies to every form of the Lord such as Rama, Narasimha and Vamana.

🎙 Question from the floor at 97:06 (auto-transcript): “Intentionally, I leave this subject for questions. Especially in South India, we have this thing. When we talk about incarnations, they say there is one Vishnu. He comes as Paraha, goes back. Natsya, goes back. Urmai, goes back. He comes as Asimai, goes back. So, he can say…”

In Jayadeva Goswami's Dasavatara-stotra every stanza addresses Keshava as the one who takes the fish, tortoise and other forms, and Krishna is not counted among the ten. Maharaj asks who that Keshava is.

🎙 Maharaj at 98:31 (auto-transcript): “We all know there is something called Dashavatara Stotra. You must have seen Dashavatara Stotra being played on the Bharatanatyam stage. In the Dashavatara Sutra, you will find that in every stanza, Keshavadrita Meena Sharira, Jai Jagadishare. Keshavadrita Kurma Sharira, Jai…”

Like the row of lamps at Diwali, all lit from one and all looking the same, the incarnations are equal in truth and any of them may be worshipped; still, one lamp lit the others, and that is Krishna. — “Because he is not his incarnation, he is incarnator.”

Though he is incarnator and all the incarnations still all are same. The example is that of during the poverty time what we do? We…”
