nodeData.topic: Day 05 · Three Modes, Karma and Chanting
nodeData.note: Bg 14.5–8, 4.17, 8.7, 18.66; SB 7.5.23, 12.3.52 · a class by HH Bhakti Padma Saurabha Pracharaka Swami. Maharaj explains material nature through three families living in goodness, passion and ignorance, and shows how our karma, earned only in human life, decides which of 84 lakh kinds of body comes next. Good and bad karma both bind; only akarma, work done for Krishna's pleasure, frees the soul from a world of birth, old age, disease and death. He then teaches the audience to chant the Hare Krishna maha-mantra on beads, leads one full round, and answers questions on desire, Tulasi and progress. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note:
Maharaj reviews Day 4: God is the source and cause of everything, and a clear idea of Brahman, Paramatma and Bhagavan removes the confusion about whether He has form.

🎙 Maharaj at 00:01 (auto-transcript): “Yesterday, we learned about who is God. When we were discussing about God, we understood the primary definition of God is to know that He is the source of everything. He is the cause of all causes. He is the creator, he is the creator, he is the creator, he is the destroyer.…”

The one sun is seen as the sun itself, as its reflection in water and as sunshine everywhere; in the same way Paramatma and Brahman depend on Bhagavan. Whoever has the six opulences in full has a personality, so God is a person with emotions, and the all-attractive one is called Krishna.

🎙 Maharaj at 01:27 (auto-transcript): “They are actually one. Like sun is one, but the same sun reflects in water as reflection. The same sun is present everywhere in the form of sunshine. So Brahman, Paramatma, Bhagavan, they are all one only. But though they are one, but the manifestation is different. Like one…”

Maharaj says other traditions also speak of angels and gods of wind and rain; the Vedic books simply describe them in detail. The demigods run departments of the world as Krishna's devotees and are to be respected, while Krishna alone is the object of worship.

🎙 Maharaj at 06:39 (auto-transcript): “So to remove that confusion, we understood yesterday that how, who is Ganesha? And who is Durga? We also understood who is Lord Shiva? As sum and substance, all the demigods, they are actually assisting Krishna in the administration of this world. They are taking care of…”

Today's subject is prakriti and karma. On Day 2 we heard that the soul leaves one body for another, so Maharaj asks: on what basis do we get the next one? A human does not automatically become a human again, nor a woman a woman.

🎙 Maharaj at 09:16 (auto-transcript): “Now, in the second day, the second day, we discussed about soul. While discussing about the soul, we talked about how the soul leaves the body at the time of death and goes to another body. Now, the question arises that based on which or based on what we get the next body? Is…”

Maharaj lists them: 9 lakh aquatics, 20 lakh plants and trees, 11 lakh insects, 10 lakh birds, 30 lakh animals and 4 lakh human kinds. He compares this with the far smaller numbers he says botanists and zoologists have catalogued.

🎙 Maharaj at 09:59 (auto-transcript): “84 lakh varieties of options we have in front of us. Padma Purana gives a description, a classification of these 84 lakh varieties. Jalajanulakshani stavaraha lakshvamshati Jaladalu lakshani means what? There are 9 lakh varieties of aquatics. And stavaraha lakshvamshati 20…”

Modern classification goes by bodily structure, such as chordates and non-chordates. The Vedic count separates species by the level of consciousness each one has.

🎙 Maharaj at 11:39 (auto-transcript): “Now only differences, the species which are described in the Vedic literature, their classification is not based on the bodily differences. It is not like chordates, non-chordates, protophoros, cylindrate, all like that There are different kinds of classifications made based…”

Which car or which clothes you can take from a shop depends on what you can pay. The next body is bought the same way, and the currency is what we have done in this life. — “it depends on how much you can pay”

🎙 Maharaj at 12:55 (auto-transcript): “now no question arises based on what we get the next body now it is a very simple thing where when you go to a shop what kind of car you can buy or if you go to a shop if you go to a clock shop what kind of clothes you can buy it depends on how much you can pay isn't it so in…”

If everyone is a soul, why do people, even twins, have such different natures and desires? Maharaj answers from the Gita: everyone is under the modes of material nature.

🎙 Maharaj at 13:37 (auto-transcript): “Now a question arises here. Why is it so that everybody is soul? Though everybody is soul, why people behave in different ways? Why people act in different ways? Why they have different natures? Why they have different desires? Not only just two people, even twins have…”
This verse names goodness, passion and ignorance as the three modes born of material nature that bind the unchanging soul in the body.

All colours and shades come from mixing yellow, red and blue in different proportions. In the same way one person may be 70% goodness, 20% passion, 10% ignorance and another 40-40-20, giving unlimited natures, desires and bodies. — “mixture of three colors yellow red and blue”

🎙 Maharaj at 15:14 (auto-transcript): “varies like for example you have so many colors in this world and each color has infinite number of shades where are these infinite colors and infinite shades coming from basically it is mixture of three colors yellow red and blue when you mix these three colors in different…”

For the sake of study Maharaj pictures a family mainly in goodness. Their mark is peace, because their formula is simple living and high thinking.

🎙 Maharaj at 17:05 (auto-transcript): “a family who is primarily in mode of goodness. A family primarily in mode of goodness conducts his life in this way. Krishna says in the Bhagavad Gita, Tatra Sattva Nirmanathvaat Prakashatma Anamayam Sutrasangera Vatnati Khyanasangena Chanaka Tatra Sattva Nirmanathvaat Sattva…”
This verse describes goodness as the purest mode, which gives light and a sense of happiness and knowledge, and binds through attachment to them.

They rise early, bathe and keep themselves and their surroundings clean. Their love stands on responsibility, not on flickering emotion that says 'I love you' one day and 'I hate you' the next.

🎙 Maharaj at 18:16 (auto-transcript): “A family in mode of goodness, they govern their life by certain principles. Their principles means they have a regulated lifestyle. And the first and foremost important principle in their life is they get up early in the morning. That is why they are in mode of goodness, that…”

The family prays and has breakfast together, the father teaches values on the way to school and works on time, neither lazy nor overworking. Outings are to scenic places or temples, they give charity, and the house holds only what is needed. — “It is said that a family which prays together, stays together.”

🎙 Maharaj at 20:07 (auto-transcript): “It is said that a family which prays together, stays together. A family which eats together, stays together. So you find these days it is not happening. Everybody has their own time. Isn't it? The mother eats at a different time. The son eats. The daughter eats at a different…”

Maharaj now turns to the family in passion, whose mark is constant anxiety, and then briefly to ignorance.

🎙 Maharaj at 22:06 (auto-transcript): “Now, we'll talk about passion. A family mode of passion is like this. Krishna talks about mode of passion. He says, Krishna says that mode of passion is symptomized by always anxiety. As much as goodness is symptomized by peace, passion is symptomized by anxiety. It means a…”

This verse says passion is born of longing and attachment and binds the soul to action. Maharaj gives the family's formula as 'money is honey': more money, more enjoyment, so they work harder and harder and the enjoyment never arrives. — “The result of hard work is hard work.”

Attachment based on passion is self-centred: it is to what the other person has, for one's own enjoyment. It is like chasing water in a mirage; ask such a person to come to a Gita class and he is 'very busy'.

🎙 Maharaj at 23:39 (auto-transcript): “Now a person in mode of passion is attached. Just imagine, always think, somebody in this world, when he is very attached to you, when she is very attached to you, you should understand this attachment if it is based on passion, it is actually not attachment to you. It is not…”

children.topic: A day that starts with a fight
children.note:
The alarm rings at six, he wakes tired because the mind planned all night, sleeps 'five more minutes' and it is 7:30; husband and wife shout, the geyser is burnt, the boss shouts, he forgets the anniversary. In the evening they recall the day they met, then the son's report card arrives and in two minutes they are quarrelling again.

🎙 Maharaj at 25:13 (auto-transcript): “Busy for what? Busy for suffering. Anyhow, so in this way, a person in mode of passion, they get up early in the morning. The husband has put up an alarm at 6 o'clock because he has to go and catch a bus or a train at 7.30. I don't know, it is not so much in Sri Lanka, but…”

Even giving and eating are coloured by the mode, and Maharaj gives two stories from his college days in Calcutta.

🎙 Maharaj at 30:57 (auto-transcript): “And sometimes they do charity also. But their charity is like this. It's a real story I'm going to tell about a person in mode of passion giving charity. I was regularly from my college in Calcutta. I used to go to Mayapur once in 15 days and stay there for a couple of days…”

The Mayapur temple president tells Maharaj of a businessman who donated fans for the temple hall. He returns asking for his name on each fan, then on all the blades and the centre, and finally asks that the fans not be run too much.

🎙 Maharaj at 31:02 (auto-transcript): “It's a real story I'm going to tell about a person in mode of passion giving charity. I was regularly from my college in Calcutta. I used to go to Mayapur once in 15 days and stay there for a couple of days and then here to different lectures and all. The president of the…”

A friend treats Maharaj at a cold air-conditioned restaurant, orders everything extra spicy, sweats with red eyes, then gulps cold water and feels relief. It is like a man kicked 25 times a day who is delighted to get only 20. — “For them happiness is nothing but the reduction of misery.”

🎙 Maharaj at 34:08 (auto-transcript): “my friend on his birthday party took me to a restaurant many years back we were in college he was a very introvert person and he had not many friends I was the only person who was very friendly with him he considered me as only friend he told I want to take you and give you a…”

This is hardly a family at all; Maharaj's example is a couple who 'try out' living together for two years, marry and divorce in six months. They rise around eleven, forget bathing, eat whatever stale thing is in the fridge and live in sleep and intoxication.

🎙 Maharaj at 36:39 (auto-transcript): “And now going further, there is mode of ignorance. A family is more of victory. This is not a family at all. They are just staying together. This is something like a new concept which has come from the West and has become very much prevalent here. That is, prevalent in India,…”
Maharaj touches this verse, which says the mode of ignorance deludes everyone and binds through negligence, laziness and sleep.

children.topic: How the law of karma works
children.note:
These three ways of living decide the next body, so Maharaj says we must understand karma properly.

🎙 Maharaj at 39:17 (auto-transcript): “So you don't want to discuss much about a person in mode of ignorance that you very well can imagine how horrible that person can be. So we have these three ways of conducting life. Based on these three ways of conducting life, our next body is defined. Our next body is…”

A mango seed gives a mango tree and paddy gives rice, never wheat. Every action brings its matching reaction; Maharaj calls it a law of nature.

🎙 Maharaj at 39:44 (auto-transcript): “of karma is very important to understand. Whatever you sow, what you reap, what you sow, you will reap. If you put a mango seed, you will get a mango tree. If you go to the field and throw the grains of paddy, then you will get rice, you will not get wheat. So whatever action…”

Someone doing wrong now but enjoying must have done good before, and a good person suffering is meeting an earlier act. 'Before' can mean this life, the last one, or three or ten lives ago.

🎙 Maharaj at 40:23 (auto-transcript): “may say that why is it so there are some people who are bad but they are getting good and some people who are good but they are getting bad it's a very interesting question why good people good things happen to bad people when bad things happen to good people why is it so it…”

Caught on CCTV, a murderer protests that the killer wore a blue shirt and he is wearing red. Changing the dress called the body excuses us just as little. — “that doesn't mean we will be exempted from the punishment”

🎙 Maharaj at 41:41 (auto-transcript): “As we have discussed before, that this body is considered to be a dress. When this dress is spoiled or torn off, you wear a new dress. In the same way, somebody committed a murder. And after 3-4 days, the police comes and arrest him. And he says, why are you arresting me? You…”

A slap is returned at once, while a murder case may run for years through courts and appeals. Vegetables fruit in months, bananas in a year or two, mangoes after five years; no fixed time is guaranteed.

🎙 Maharaj at 42:39 (auto-transcript): “The reactions may come in any lifetime. Sometimes for a small crime or for a small mistake or a small bad activity, the reaction comes immediately. Sometimes for a gross crime, a big crime, the reactions come maybe after years, who knows. Like we have a, we know that example,…”
Maharaj quotes this verse to say that the ways of action, wrong action and inaction are intricate and not straightforward.

Good deeds do not cancel bad ones; each gives its own result. Two sinful men both become dogs, but the one who also gave charity rides in a Mercedes with costly shampoo and biscuits, while the other lies on the street and is run over by that same car. — “Karma can never be neutralized.”

🎙 Maharaj at 44:21 (auto-transcript): “And that is why we have an idea, some people think that, okay, I have done some bad activity, what I will do, I will do some good and I will neutralize them, but it doesn't happen like that. If you have done any activity, whether good or bad, definitely you have to pay the…”

A tiger killing a deer acts by instinct and gets no bad karma; only the human being has the freedom to choose what to do. Eating, sleeping, mating and defending are done better by animals: gymnasts train from childhood to do what a monkey does naturally.

🎙 Maharaj at 46:33 (auto-transcript): “so that is why it should be understood that karma is earned only in the human form of life suppose a tiger eats or kills a deer so the tiger or the lion doesn't get the bad karma for it Why? Because it is the instinctive nature of the tiger or the lion to do so. That is why…”

A pilot decides to drive his plane on the road, and the police tell him to take a small car, because a plane is meant to take off. — “human life is meant to take off from this material world”

🎙 Maharaj at 47:57 (auto-transcript): “human life is meant to actually get out of the world that is what we discussed the first day like for example sometimes somebody who was trained as a pilot no every day was flying one day he thought why to fly today i want to take the airplane on the road he comes out at or…”

We can go down to lower species, up to higher ones, be human again, or go back home to the spiritual world and never take birth here again.

🎙 Maharaj at 50:29 (auto-transcript): “There is a choice. What is a choice we have? There are four choices we have in the next life. life either go to lower species number one either go to higher species number two number three you take the human birth again number four that you go back home back to world to…”

Does doing good take us to the spiritual world? No, says Maharaj: good karma and bad karma both bind us here. The Gita adds a third kind, akarma, action with no reaction.

🎙 Maharaj at 51:05 (auto-transcript): “If I do good, will I go to the spiritual world? No. What to speak of? Even just by doing some good activities, pious activities that also will not guarantee that we are going to go back home, back to Godhead. Why? Because both good karma and bad karma, both are binding to…”

Pious work is like building a bank balance: you enjoy until it runs down, then come back to work again. Unlawful acts create a negative balance, which has to be suffered.

🎙 Maharaj at 51:57 (auto-transcript): “So let us try to understand these three kinds of karmas The first karma we know very well It is good activity, pious activity By which we can enjoy in this life or in the next life It is like accumulating a bank balance by working hard Once your bank balance becomes…”

In a huge department store one man takes goods and pays (karma), another steals and goes to jail (vikarma). A third walks out without paying, because he is the owner's servant and takes everything for the owner; so a devotee's acts for Krishna's pleasure carry no reaction.

🎙 Maharaj at 53:22 (auto-transcript): “have a big departmental store, huge, I don't know, here you can sit as come or not. They There are huge, you can get fright from vegetables till super computers there. Everything you get in that. So, you go in that, whatever you want, you take it. When you come out, you pay…”

Burnt seeds do not sprout even when planted and watered; knowledge and work for Krishna burn the seed of reaction. If merely doing one's duty were karma-yoga, a donkey would be a karma-yogi; yoga means connection, so it is work that connects us with Krishna.

🎙 Maharaj at 54:51 (auto-transcript): “reaction. All the reactions are burnt. Like the seeds, when they are burnt, even though you put them in the ground and pour water, it doesn't give rise to any further fruits. So the reaction, the seed or the reaction is burnt by the power of knowledge, by the power of…”

Maharaj says Duryodhana ruled well, gave charity to brahmanas, protected the citizens and was later seen in heaven. Yet Krishna did not want him as king, because he did his duty for his own pleasure, with himself at the centre. — “The problem is whom are you doing it for?”

🎙 Maharaj at 56:08 (auto-transcript): “we will have a better understanding when we know about Duryodhana and the Pandavas. Duryodhana, he was he was he doing some bad activities no he was a perfect king he was executing all his responsibilities he was treating the brahmins giving charity to the brahmins he was…”

Maharaj points to the Gita's concluding call in 18.66 to give up all dharmas and says the book is therefore not a book of religion. Piety may bring a comfortable or wealthy life, but it does not take us beyond this world. — “Bhagavad Gita is a book of spiritual science.”

Why go to the spiritual world at all? Because, Maharaj says, this world is full of misery and is not a fit place for the soul, however hard we try to be happy here.

🎙 Maharaj at 59:27 (auto-transcript): “Now somebody may say, why we should go to the spiritual world? Because this material world is full of misery. And this is not the fit place for the soul to stay. The soul, we can never be happy in this world. In spite of all the prayasa, in spite of all the efforts to be…”

By nature's law we undergo birth, death, old age and disease, and on top of these the miseries caused by our own body and mind, by other beings and by nature. He recalls Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Thakura saying this world is not a fit place for a gentleman.

🎙 Maharaj at 59:54 (auto-transcript): “Because by nature's law, we have to undergo birth, death, old age and disease. And not only these four, we have adhi-atmika kleshas, adhi-bhautika kleshas, adhi-daivika kleshas. These seven kinds of mysteries, birth, death, old age and disease. Added to that, adhi-atmika,…”

The first thing a newborn does is cry, and everyone around laughs; if the baby is peaceful they pinch him to make him cry. Before that come nine cramped months in the womb. — “You cry and others laugh.”

🎙 Maharaj at 60:25 (auto-transcript): “And somebody may say, oh why are you saying birth is so horrible? What is the first thing the child does when he comes out, baby does when he comes out? Cries, isn't it? Is he happy? And the most interesting part is, when the baby comes out crying, what others do? That is how…”

children.topic: Born with a twin called death
children.note:
Along with birth a certificate of death is issued. Maharaj compares us to a man with a gun at his head and a fine plate of food in front of him, still saying 'I want to enjoy'.

🎙 Maharaj at 61:35 (auto-transcript): “As soon as you are born, along with birth, death is also born. who is the younger brother of us, there is one younger brother who is born, there is a twin who is born along with us, as soon as you are born, there is already a certificate given, you are going to die one day,…”

Maharaj cites Krishna's instruction to Arjuna to think of Him always and carry out his duty of fighting. Arjuna did not want the war but fought for Krishna; so a student, a businessman or a householder can act for Krishna, and the home becomes Krishna's household.

Renunciation has little to do with spirituality; connecting with Krishna is what counts. Connecting through work is karma-yoga, through knowledge jnana-yoga, and these lead to pure devotional service, bhakti-yoga.

🎙 Maharaj at 64:29 (auto-transcript): “What is spiritual means, when you connect yourself with Krishna, that is called spirituality. When you connect through work, it is called Karma Yoga. When you connect through your knowledge, when you connect to Krishna through knowledge, that is known as Jnana Yoga. And…”

Asked by his father Hiranyakasipu for the best thing he has learned, five-year-old Prahlada lists nine practices beginning with hearing and chanting about the Lord. Maharaj says the first two are topmost and are combined in one special meditation anyone can do.

This verse says that what meditation gave in Satya-yuga, sacrifice in Treta and temple worship in Dvapara is obtained in Kali-yuga by chanting the names of Hari. Maharaj says this practical method is what Srila Prabhupada has given us.

Astanga-yoga is meant to still the agitation of consciousness and begins with yama and niyama, yet today it is sold for health and worse. Pranayama beside a busy Bombay road only takes in more fumes, and there are no forests left to practise in.

🎙 Maharaj at 68:15 (auto-transcript): “people used to do Ashtanga Yoga. Many people asked this question about, what about Ashtanga Yoga? It is so difficult to perform in Ashtanga Yoga. just imagine Yama and Niyama it is that itself cannot be performed these days these days as the name of yoga so much is being sold…”

The great fire sacrifices of Treta need qualified brahmanas and pure ghee, which Maharaj says are hard to find in Kali-yuga. The grand temple worship of Dvapara is likewise beyond us, as the huge South Indian temples show.

🎙 Maharaj at 70:32 (auto-transcript): “And in the Treta Yoga, people used to do big, big fire sacrifices, like that, they used to chant Vedic Padras and some sacrifices. In the Dwapara Yoga, Dwapara Yoga means in Dwapara, that is just the previous age, Dwapara Paricharyaya, what is the meaning of Paricharyaya?…”

People think yoga is standing upside down, producing ash by magic or growing a beard in the forest. When Maharaj asks morning meditators whom they meditate on, they do not know and are really sleeping; the best object is Krishna, and the simplest way is to chant His names.

🎙 Maharaj at 72:30 (auto-transcript): “mantra. This is the topmost yoga system. Many people, they are very much carried away with this yoga. They think yoga means standing upside down. But definitely yoga doesn't mean stand upside down. Or sometimes people think yoga means to do some mystical activity, some magic.…”

Maharaj teaches everyone to chant the Hare Krishna maha-mantra on the japa beads they have been given. Morning is best, but any free and peaceful time will do, provided the time is exclusive: not while watching TV or cooking.

🎙 Maharaj at 74:00 (auto-transcript): “the most convenient in the age of Kali. So we'll be teaching you today how to chant the Hare Krishna Mahamantra to all of you. There is a particular method we have to chant it and it can be done by everyone and surprisingly you can do this chanting of the Hare Krishna…”

The special bead on top is the Meru or Krishna bead. The index finger, tarjani, does not touch the beads; Maharaj says it is the finger of fault-finding and works like an antenna that brings the criticised fault back to oneself, and recalls his mother correcting him for pointing as a child.

🎙 Maharaj at 74:52 (auto-transcript): “i hope all of you have got the jatmalas so in the jatmala which has been given to you it has got a special bead on top it is called meru or is also known as krishna bead this is a special one hold it with your don't touch the bead with your pointing finger Don't touch the…”

Holding the Krishna bead, all repeat the Panca-tattva mantra after him. The maha-mantra was given by Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu and His associates, so we first ask their blessings and pardon for mistakes in chanting.

🎙 Maharaj at 77:33 (auto-transcript): “And now holding this Jatmala, this particular bead, we chant one mantra called the Panchatatta Pranam Mantra. In the piece of paper which has been given to you, there is one mantra in the Mangalachan verses, there is one mantra, the last but one, Yabodha Hare Krishna Mantra.…”

On each bead the whole mantra is chanted once, and devotees go around checking how people hold the beads. The hall chants all 108 beads together; for the next round the beads are turned around without crossing the Krishna bead.

🎙 Maharaj at 79:04 (auto-transcript): “So after chanting the Pancha Tattva Manava Mantra, you go to the next field, called the next field, and then chant the Hare Krishna Manava Mantra now after me. A couple of devotees can see whether they are chanting properly or not, turning the beats properly or not. So hold…”

If the mind wanders, do not worry. Attend to only two things, saying every syllable properly and hearing every syllable properly, and the mind will come under control.

🎙 Maharaj at 88:51 (auto-transcript): “So, this Hare Krishna Maha Mantra, when you are chanting, some people say, my mind goes here and there. Don't worry about it. You just have to worry about one thing, two things rather. Number one, whether you are pronouncing every syllable properly or not. Number two, whether…”

A round takes seven or eight minutes with practice, about ten at first. Everyone is to chant two rounds before tomorrow's class, giving those twenty minutes with no phone calls or talking, and bring the beads back.

🎙 Maharaj at 89:26 (auto-transcript): “So to chant this Hare Krishna mantra, to chant one round, it takes around seven to eight minutes. Initially for the first one week or ten days, since you are not in practice, it may take ten minutes. but to chant one round after some days or few days of practice it takes only…”

Maharaj closes the talk a little over time and takes questions from the audience on the day's class.

🎙 Maharaj at 90:48 (auto-transcript): “So today we will end the session. Before we end the session, any questions please to ask. I know we are just over time a little bit. How much is the time? Any questions? So please bring the Jatmanas tomorrow. Keep it with you and bring it tomorrow. And everybody will chant…”

children.topic: Q1 · How to stay in goodness?
children.note:
The modes keep changing: goodness in the morning, passion in the afternoon, ignorance at night. To stay in goodness, lead a regulated life whose pivot is rising early, finishing bath and bathroom within half an hour or so, and then sitting to chant; food habits will be discussed tomorrow.

🎙 Question from the floor at 91:08 (auto-transcript): “Yes. Definitely the modes are always changing. Morning you are in goodness, afternoon in passion, night in ignorance. And it always changes. That is the nature. I already told that modes are always changing. But predominantly somebody may be in passion and ignorance and…”

children.topic: Why not cross the Krishna bead?
children.note:
The Meru bead stands for Krishna in the middle of the 108 beads and is treated as sacred, so we do not step over it. Maharaj says this is a tradition and not a philosophical point.

🎙 Maharaj at 93:14 (auto-transcript): “so here it is considered to be meru it is krishna being like something very sacred you don't cross over it that is the reason it is considered krishna is the middle and the 108 copies are there so it is a it's just a tradition there is no real philosophical understanding of…”

children.topic: Q2 · Why did we come here?
children.note:
If we were happy in the spiritual world, why are we in this one? Maharaj calls it the last question anyone can ask, and says the main thing is to think of getting out.

🎙 Question from the floor at 93:39 (auto-transcript): “tradition yeah why are we in the physical world is so happy in the spiritual world this is the last question anybody can ask if somebody starts thinking about different different things. Then they land up into this question. Once somebody knows the answer to this question,…”

children.topic: Free people still land in jail
children.note:
Citizens are free and happy, yet some commit crimes and go to jail; an intelligent one, once out, does not go back. As parts of Krishna we have a minute tendency to lord it over, and when free will is misused we are sent here to try, until by good fortune we meet a devotee and remember we are not the Lord.

🎙 Maharaj at 94:25 (auto-transcript): “spiritual world, why he came here? You see, there is a jail in Sri Lanka and Colombo, there must be jail. People are quite happy, they are quite free, but still people go to jail, isn't it? But if that person is intelligent, once he comes out of the jail, he will not go back.…”

children.topic: Q3 · Why strive? Give up desires?
children.note:
One person asks why we work so hard for success if all is to be given up, and another whether giving up all desires makes one spiritual. Maharaj says the soul's nature is to desire; material desires cannot satisfy us because we are not matter. — “we are asking you to have spiritual desires”

🎙 Question from the floor at 96:16 (auto-transcript): “second question is why do we achieve so much of success if you give it all if if we give why are we striving hard to achieve success if we have to give it all anyway. That is my question too. That is why this whole soul, whole course is meant for. To any way to give up all.…”

Sing and dance with Krishna's names in the temple, relish prasadam instead of restaurants, build something big such as the temple in Colombo, call this seven-day course and the coming Kartik month a party. Want to teach? Teach Bhagavad-gita, where there is little competition; want drama, there are many about Krishna.

🎙 Maharaj at 97:55 (auto-transcript): “There you may ask, what is spiritual desire? Everybody has a desire to sing and dance. So instead of singing and dancing in a party where ultimately people get frustrated and come out, you sing and dance in the temple in a satsana program with Krishna's names. To have a…”

She is addressed as Tulasi Devi, not a plant, for she bestows devotion and Krishna accepts nothing without her. Maharaj tells how Satyabhama piled all her gold on the scale against Krishna without moving it, and Rukmini balanced Him with a single Tulasi leaf.

🎙 Question from the floor at 100:36 (auto-transcript): “So other question was, speak something about Thulasi plant. So we don't say Thulasi plant, we address her as Thulasi Devi, Thulasi Maharani. Because she is not just a plant. She is a Devi, she is a Bhakti Devi. So she gives devotion. She is the one who bestows devotion.…”

A listener objects that cars and every discovery came from passionate people, so what happens to progress if all aim for the spiritual world? Maharaj welcomes the question.

🎙 Question from the floor at 102:37 (auto-transcript): “So much of progress in humanity, all that would stop and only nothing more gets discovered, nothing more gets invented. The rest of the things we have in life is because people were passionate about it. So much was achieved, let's say even the automobile technology people…”

Progress means movement towards a goal. In Maharaj's view much technology, the internet included, was first developed for military use and only later reached the public, so he asks where it is really heading. — “So are we really progressing?”

🎙 Maharaj at 103:10 (auto-transcript): “So are we really progressing? Okay, if we are progressing towards what? When we say progress, we are actually talking about progress in a particular direction, to a particular goal, isn't it? Definitely we are progressing. But towards what? Towards self-destruction. Every…”

A person in goodness also uses cars, phones and computers, but for a proper purpose and in a regulated way; passion overuses and ignorance destroys. He mentions people forgetting whom they dialled after two rings and children who cannot multiply 13 by 14 without a calculator.

🎙 Maharaj at 105:11 (auto-transcript): “Okay, forget this ideology and we'll just take it as a face value. This progress is giving comfort. It is all because of passion. Now, a person in mode of goodness also uses cards, mobiles, etc, etc. but he use it for a proper purpose, use it in a regulated way that is why we…”

Maharaj points to the Ranganatha and Madurai temples as signs of an advanced older science, and says ISKCON freely uses management and IT. He names Narayana Murthy as someone who built a large company while living simply and without anxiety.

🎙 Maharaj at 109:05 (auto-transcript): “another explanation. When you say, you are just thinking of cards and some progress. If you think in the previous days when more people were spiritual and Vedic, there were no signs. There were higher quality of signs. Ask them to build one Ranganatha temple. The entire…”

Asked by a student in Baroda why he renounced society, Maharaj replies that he attends seven parties a week. Nothing is ours to renounce anyway; put Krishna in the centre and the bad elements leave on their own. — “you add Krishna to your life”

🎙 Maharaj at 112:40 (auto-transcript): “So person who is renounced can also create. As I have told during my lecture, renunciation has little to do with spirituality. nodeData.topic: Day 06 · Five Do's and Four Don'ts
nodeData.note: Bg 7.2, 18.65 · a class by HH Bhakti Padma Saurabha Pracharaka Swami. The closing class turns the Bhagavad-gita into a daily programme. Maharaj first shows that the Gita is a manual for life, meant for busy householders today, then gives the five chief practices taught by Lord Caitanya - devotees' company, the holy name, daily reading, a holy place and Deity worship - and the four things to avoid. He ends with the fourfold satisfaction of Krishna consciousness and answers questions on Buddha, the Bhagavatam, akarma, the history of ISKCON and time. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note:
Maharaj opens the last session by recalling yesterday's class on how karma works, what material nature is, and how the next life is decided. He then sets today's theme: the practical application of the Bhagavad-gita, as three questions - what to do, why to do it, and how to do it.

🎙 Maharaj at 00:00 (auto-transcript): “Aray Krishna. So welcome to our last session for today. Now yesterday we discussed about how karma functions. What is Prakriti? And based on what we get the next life. We understood how Prakriti is made up of three modes of nature. Sattva guna, Raju guna and Dhamma guna. They…”

children.topic: The modes decide the next life
children.note:
A life led in goodness takes one to the higher planets, passion brings a human birth in the middle planets, and ignorance leads to the lower species. So it matters very much which mode we choose to act in.

🎙 Maharaj at 00:25 (auto-transcript): “Krishna says in the Bhagavad Gita that the next life is dependent on what kind of modes in which we are living in, what kind of modes we conduct our life. If we conduct our life in mode of goodness, if we conduct our life in mode of goodness then we go to higher planetary…”

children.topic: Good deeds do not cancel bad
children.note:
Every action has its reaction, in this life or some later one, and pious acts do not wipe out sinful ones - both must be experienced. Maharaj recalls the two dogs: one born a dog and also hurt in an accident, the other a dog by its sins yet enjoying comfort because of some piety.

🎙 Maharaj at 01:45 (auto-transcript): “So some people have this idea that by doing some good activities or pious activities, I can nullify the impious or the sinful activities. It doesn't happen like that. We need to experience both good and bad. So every action, whether good or bad, has to be experienced. We get…”

Beyond good and bad work there is akarma, action that brings no reaction. It is the same business, the same singing, the same daily work, only done for Krishna; this is karma-yoga, and as attachment to Krishna grows it becomes bhakti-yoga with its nine activities, of which hearing and chanting are the chief. He reminds everyone of the homework: two rounds of japa. — “Whatever normally you are doing in your life, just do the same thing.”

🎙 Maharaj at 02:54 (auto-transcript): “So what is that? That is known as Akarma. Yesterday we discussed about Akarma. What is the meaning of Akarma? Akarma means that activity which is beyond good and bad are those activities which do not have any reactions. And what are those activities? It is the same activities…”

children.topic: The Gita is meant to be lived
children.note:
Before listing the do's and don'ts, Maharaj explains why application matters. To know and not act is to see without seeing and hear without hearing.

🎙 Maharaj at 05:44 (auto-transcript): “But before we actually talk about what to do and what not to do, then we will actually discuss about how practical application is a very important aspect of Bhagavad Gita. It is like you know, but if you don't act on it, then it is called stilly prudence. Pashanavimapashati.…”

A man takes a cigarette from a packet that plainly says smoking injures health. Ask him if he wants to injure his health and he says no - yet he smokes. Maharaj calls this the picture of ignorance we have to come out of. — “So this is called ignorance.”

🎙 Maharaj at 06:12 (auto-transcript): “Like the famous example which I always give is a person who is taking a cigarette out of a cigarette packet. So on the cigarette packet it is written, cigarette smoking is injurious to health. It is cancerous. It is written there. But still he smokes. And you ask the person,…”

Krishna promises Arjuna both knowledge and its realised, practical side, after which nothing more remains to be known. Maharaj compares arts and science students: the science students stay longer in college because they have practicals, and the Gita is that kind of science, to be tested on oneself and not left to armchair philosophers.

Some accept the Gita as practical but only for Arjuna's time. Maharaj answers that it is an eternal scripture: Arjuna between the two armies trembled, burned and choked with all the signs of stress, and we meet the same condition in our own lives.

🎙 Maharaj at 08:35 (auto-transcript): “Now some people have this idea, okay Bhagavad Gita is practical, but it was practical 5000 years back, not now. It was 5000 years back where Krishna spoke the Bhagavad Gita to Arjuna in the battlefield of Kurukshetra. That was applicable at that time. Now where the modern…”

Arjuna had vowed to kill anyone who told him to give up his Gandiva bow, and one day in the war Yudhisthira, hurt and humiliated, said exactly that. Krishna resolves it by having Arjuna speak harshly to his brother, since for a kshatriya insult is worse than death. Yet this same bow slipped from Arjuna's hand before the battle - like the pen slipping from a student's hand when he reads the question paper.

🎙 Maharaj at 10:12 (auto-transcript): “Gandiva was so dear to Arjuna that he had taken a vow. Krishna had taken, Arjuna had taken a vow. So, anybody who tells me to give up Gandiva, I am going to kill him. But it so happened that on the battlefield once, there was a heavy fight between one of the days, it was 18…”

Knowing that hydrogen and oxygen make water changes nothing; everyone drinks water anyway. Real practicality is knowing how to face hard situations. We study matter and forget to study life, like a student entering a laboratory without knowing chemistry, or someone running a machine without reading the manual. — “That is why Bhagavad Gita is a textbook for life.”

🎙 Maharaj at 14:13 (auto-transcript): “Whatever knowledge we get these days, what is the use of the practicality? There is no practicality in that. Now as a student studying the science, oxygen, hydrogen makes water. Even if you don't know, still you are getting water and drinking water now. So those who are not…”

To those who say they will read the Gita after giving up job and family, Maharaj points to its first student: Arjuna was a ruler with heavy responsibility and a householder. And it was spoken in the middle of a battlefield, which shows that our life too is a battle and studying the Gita is the one real emergency. — “Bhagavad Gita is meant for the most responsible person.”

🎙 Maharaj at 16:18 (auto-transcript): “And some people say, it is true, Bhagavad Gita is practical, but it is for renunciates. Those who are given up their family life, those who are wonks, and those who are like in Himalayas or in some forest cities for them. But I am in household affairs. I have to do my job, I…”

Maharaj now turns to what we are supposed to do, beginning from the verse he calls the secret of the Gita and from Lord Caitanya, who showed how to live it.

🎙 Maharaj at 18:43 (auto-transcript): “Now, after discussing why we have to practically apply Bhagavad Gita, then we'll go to what we are supposed to do. Now, when we talk about what we are supposed to do, we should understand that in Bhagavad Gita Krishna told, Man mana bhava madbhakto madhyaji maam namaskuru…”

Krishna asks Arjuna to think of Him, become His devotee, worship Him and bow to Him. Maharaj says that although millions of copies of the Gita are printed and read, this simple point remains a secret because readers miss what Krishna actually wanted to say.

children.topic: Krishna comes as His own devotee
children.note:
Few studied the Gita, fewer understood, and fewer still applied it. So the same Krishna appeared about 500 years ago as Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu - the name the class chanted in the Panca-tattva mantra - in the form of His own devotee, constantly chanting and in tears, to show what love of God means. — “Just giving a lecture would not make people understand.”

🎙 Maharaj at 20:15 (auto-transcript): “That is why the same Krishna had to appear just 500 years back in the form of Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu. Like when yesterday I gave you the Mahamantra, Hare Krishna Mahamantra. Before you chanted the Hare Krishna Mahamantra, you chanted the mantra called Panchatattu…”

children.topic: A lecture on halwa is not enough
children.note:
If you only lecture on how to make halwa, nobody can make it afterwards; take them into the kitchen and show them, and they can. Krishna gave the lecture, and as Lord Caitanya He took us into the kitchen.

🎙 Maharaj at 21:02 (auto-transcript): “Like for example, if you give a lecture to people, how to make halwa or how to make some eatable or some item. So if you give a lecture, after that you ask everyone who won't make it, they will not be able to make it. So if you take them to the kitchen and then show them this…”

Maharaj says Lord Caitanya taught sixty-four items of devotional service and then named five as the most important. These five are today's do's: association with devotees, chanting the holy name, hearing the Bhagavad-gita and Srimad-Bhagavatam, living in a holy place, and serving the Deity.

🎙 Maharaj at 22:20 (auto-transcript): “So, Shri Chaitanya Mahabhu, while he was explaining Bhagavan Goswami, he says there are 64 items of devotional service. 64 points he told about what we are supposed to do. But after speaking about the 64 points, he says among all the 64, 5 are the most important. They are…”

The first of the five is sadhu-sanga, associating with devotees. Maharaj explains who a sadhu is, what his company does, and three practical ways to have it.

🎙 Maharaj at 23:23 (auto-transcript): “Now let us see how to do these five things in our life. The first one, Sadhu Sangha. What is the meaning of Sadhu Sangha? Sadhu Sangha means to assure sacred devotees. Let us understand what is Sadhu. What is the meaning of Sadhu? Sadhu means a devotee of Krishna. He is…”

A sadhu is known by qualities, not by dress. From Lord Kapila's talk with Devahuti Maharaj lists them: tolerant like a tree that still gives shade and fruit when its branches are cut, compassionate even to one who hurt him, a friend to all with no enemies, peaceful, and living by scripture. The most inward quality is that he will do anything for Krishna's sake.
Maharaj quotes the Caitanya-caritamrita verse saying all scriptures praise sadhu-sanga and that even a moment of it brings all perfection. He then shows it from history and from recent times.

The hunter Mrigari half-killed animals because he enjoyed watching them struggle. Narada tells him it is sinful and that Krishna will maintain him if he gives up hunting. Mrigari and his wife simply chant; villagers bring so much food that he feeds everyone, and when Narada returns, the same man steps carefully so as not to crush the ants.

🎙 Maharaj at 26:19 (auto-transcript): “association attain perfection? It has been seen in the history, in the Bhagavatam days discretion of a very cruel hunter. His name was Braghari. This Braghari used to take pleasure when the animals used to suffer. Sometimes, not sometimes, many a times, Braghari used to half…”

To those who say such things are only in the Puranas, Maharaj gives Srila Prabhupada, who went to America at about seventy. Young people sunk in drugs, he says, gave up meat, intoxicants and even tea and coffee through his company.

🎙 Maharaj at 31:25 (auto-transcript): “Now you may say, oh that is all in the books, in the Puranas, but nowadays where? It has been seen practically in the life of Srila Prabhupada. In his divine days, A.C. Bhaktivedanta, Swami Srila Prabhupada. He went to America at the age of 69, at the age of 70 he went to…”

children.topic: Tell me who your friend is
children.note:
As a child Maharaj would come home from play and his mother would ask whom he had played with; if it was a notorious boy, he was not allowed back. The consciousness of our companions flows into us, so choosing our company is the one thing to be careful about. — “That is the turning point in your life.”

🎙 Maharaj at 32:31 (auto-transcript): “So we find sadhu sangha. The association of sadhu is so much that it transforms the life of a person. Actually association matters a lot in everyone's life. I always remember in my childhood, whenever I used to play, go down and play and used to come back to the house, my…”

Srila Prabhupada opened Radha-Krishna temples all over the world, and Maharaj says their whole purpose is to be a platform where people can meet devotees - including the temple being built in Colombo.

🎙 Maharaj at 33:50 (auto-transcript): “So now Srila Prabhupada says the entire purpose of our temples is to give association to devotees. That is the whole purpose of Krishna consciousness movement. Srila Prabhupada opened temples of Krishna, Radha Krishna around the world. Now you go even Australia you will find…”

Maharaj gives a practical programme for sadhu-sanga at three levels.

🎙 Maharaj at 35:05 (auto-transcript): “Now you may say, okay, associate with devotees, what is the practical purpose you have for us so that we can associate with devotees? When you see association, there is association with devotees at three levels. The first level of association is to associate with Śrīla…”

children.topic: With Srila Prabhupada, through his mission
children.note:
We associate with Srila Prabhupada by helping his mission of spreading Krishna consciousness: telling one more person about the temple, giving someone a Bhagavad-gita. A child or an old man can do this; it is not a duty of a few monks.

🎙 Maharaj at 35:19 (auto-transcript): “The first level of association is to associate with Śrīla Prabhupāda because there is no sadhu which the world has seen in the recent past who is as efficient as Prabhupāda, as wonderful as Śrīla Prabhupāda. And how do we associate with Prabhupāda? We can associate with Śrīla…”

The second level is to attend a weekly class in the temple or nearby and take practical guidance from a senior Vaishnava who knows the scriptures. He mentions the Sunday afternoon programme in the temple, held in Tamil.

🎙 Maharaj at 36:59 (auto-transcript): “The first level of association. The second level of association is to attend a weekly program which happens in the temple and in the nearby places in your city, in your town. So this is association of an advanced Vaishnava who has some more experience of scriptures, who is…”

children.topic: Friendly to all, friends with devotees
children.note:
The third and most important level: be friendly with everyone, but count only devotees as real friends, because we go where a friend takes us. Maharaj says he is friendly to everyone on trains and flights, without any ill will, yet keeps this distinction. — “So a sadhu is friendly to everyone.”

🎙 Maharaj at 38:20 (auto-transcript): “now the third association is the most important what is the most important the third association the third association is to actually be friends with only devotees others you can be friendly there is a lot of difference considering one person to be friend and being friendly…”

Maharaj says ninety-nine per cent of spiritual progress rests on chanting the Hare Krishna maha-mantra and everything else is the remaining one per cent. Only two things need care: pronouncing every syllable and hearing every syllable; morning is best, and nothing else should be done alongside.

🎙 Maharaj at 41:18 (auto-transcript): “Now the second one, that is Harina. Chanting the names of Krishna. The Hare Krishna Mahamudra what has been given to you yesterday. The chanting of the Hare Krishna Mahamudra is 99% of spiritual progress is based on chanting the Hare Krishna Mahamudra. There is no other…”

In earlier ages people went to the forest for meditation and yoga, but in this age the mind is too disturbed for that. Maharaj recites the Upanishad verse on the sixteen names and says all the Vedic texts point to this one remedy.

🎙 Maharaj at 41:53 (auto-transcript): “There are so many other processes of self-realization, but that is not meant for the age of Kali. In the age of Krita Yuga or Satya Yuga people used to do Dhyan, go to the forest and do all kinds of Rashtanga and yogic practices, but that is not possible now because our mind…”

children.topic: Why we are called Hare Krishnas
children.note:
Srila Prabhupada went with only a pair of kartals and the pure name changed people. The society is ISKCON, yet the world calls the devotees Hare Krishnas - they answer the phone with it, and even when annoyed they say "Hare Krishna, Prabhu". Landing in Colombo, Maharaj was greeted with "Hare Krishna" by airport workers. — “Because we always chant.”

🎙 Maharaj at 43:57 (auto-transcript): “That is why we find Srila Prabhupada went with a pair of Kartals, that's all. he started chanting and the influence was so much tremendous that even those people were so much into drugs just by hearing the pure holy names of the Lord they all got purified that is so much so…”

children.topic: Gopal Guru: no place is unfit
children.note:
There is no restriction of time, place or condition for chanting. Maharaj tells how Lord Caitanya once held His tongue on the way to the toilet so as not to chant in an unclean place, and a small boy asked what would happen if He left His body just then. The Lord was so pleased that He named the boy Gopal Guru.

🎙 Maharaj at 46:11 (auto-transcript): “Once what's happened, Chaitanya Mahabharu was going to morning activities, going to the toilet, morning. At that time, he was holding his tongue and going. Then one small boy asked to Chaitanya Mahaprabhu, what are you doing? Mahaprabhu told, you see my tongue constantly…”

A devotee chants in two ways. In sankirtan with mridanga and kartals one gains from everyone's chanting, hearing ten voices instead of one. In japa one sits alone with beads each day; this, Maharaj says, is the meditation meant for this age.

🎙 Maharaj at 47:27 (auto-transcript): “There are two ways of chanting the Hare Krishna mantra. A devotee should involve in both the ways. One is by Sankirtan. When devotees get together and then do Kirtan with Nudankarthal. And in this way what happens? Not only you will be benefited by your chanting, you will be…”

The remaining three do's are daily reading of the Bhagavad-gita and Srimad-Bhagavatam, living in a holy place, and worshipping the Deity. Maharaj shows how each can be done at home.

🎙 Maharaj at 49:15 (auto-transcript): “The third thing is to read books of Sri Prabhupada. read Bhagavad Gita and Bhagavatam. You may say, oh I am chanting, why I should read? I've heard some philosophy, that's enough. But it is not enough. One has to read. Because when you read, what happens, so many doubts which…”

Chanting is not a reason to skip reading: knowledge is the sword that cuts doubts, our own and other people's. The mind says "first I will solve my problems", which is like saying one will take the medicine after getting well. Even without understanding, keep reading - the Gita is not different from Krishna and He gives the understanding. Fix a time or a few verses, and hear lectures online as well. — “If you are not well, that is why you should take the medicine.”

🎙 Maharaj at 49:19 (auto-transcript): “read Bhagavad Gita and Bhagavatam. You may say, oh I am chanting, why I should read? I've heard some philosophy, that's enough. But it is not enough. One has to read. Because when you read, what happens, so many doubts which come in our own mind, and in the mind of others,…”

Spiritual life is like moving against the flow of water and needs strength. Friends and relatives who said nothing while we did wrong become anxious the moment we take to Krishna consciousness; conviction to stand firm and to convince others comes from study.

🎙 Maharaj at 53:40 (auto-transcript): “It is like going against the flow of water. Then for that you require a lot of strength. Where do you get the determination, the strength from? As soon as you take a Krishna consciousness, the people who are around you, your friends, your relatives, they are the first people…”

In his college days the family sent Maharaj's grandmother, who was free with him, to stop his reading. She shut the book and asked whether this was the age for such things. He asked whether it should be after fifty or sixty - and she left, being past sixty herself. — “She was already 60.”

🎙 Maharaj at 54:22 (auto-transcript): “Like when I still remember, just after my, during my college time, when I was reading Bhagavad Gita, at that time, all my parents and others who were very, my relatives and all, they became very suspicious about me. What is this happening to him? And it was my relationship…”

children.topic: Make your home a holy place
children.note:
Dhama-vasa does not mean everyone must move to Mathura or Dvaraka. A holy place is where everything reminds you of Krishna, as the river and trees do in Vrindavan; so fill the house with His pictures, even the computer screen. Visit a holy place when you can, and the temple weekly - Maharaj calls ISKCON temples embassies of Vrindavan, with one in Colombo.

🎙 Maharaj at 56:33 (auto-transcript): “to do. That is study of Bhagavad Gita. Now the fourth one. What is the fourth one which you are supposed to do? The fourth activity we are supposed to do is Dhamvas. Dhamvas means residing in a holy place. So that means everybody has to run to Mathura, Grundavan, Dwarka.…”

Not everyone can keep a Deity, but everyone can keep pictures of Krishna, the line of teachers and Srila Prabhupada on an altar; the weekly programmes teach how to set it up.

🎙 Maharaj at 60:07 (auto-transcript): “And the fourth one, or the fifth one, one should do is worshipping the deity of the Lord, worshipping Sri Vikraha. So not everybody can have a deity in their house, but one should have at least some photographs. Photographs of Krishna and the Guru Parambara and Srila…”

A house without Krishna is haunted, Maharaj says, and the ghost is the television: the child does not hear his mother, five people sit together without talking. He does not blame the set but the viewer, whom the advertisers persuade to buy what he does not need. — “It is an idiot's box.”

🎙 Maharaj at 60:37 (auto-transcript): “If you don't have Krishna in your house, it is like a haunted house. You may say how is it? My man, your house is not haunted. Yes, it is haunted. Because there is one ghost in every house. I don't have to tell what is that. You know very well. What is that? It's a TV. It's a…”

children.topic: Krishna as head of the house
children.note:
Husband, wife and children each think they are the centre and should be obeyed, so there is a fight. When Krishna is placed in the centre, each thinks of serving the Lord, and rising, eating and recreation all become regulated.

🎙 Maharaj at 62:19 (auto-transcript): “fight going on in every house everybody is thinking that they are the center of the house but the real person when krishna comes to the center of the house when krishna who is a real lord of the house comes there then everybody everything is in space otherwise what people…”

Worship is according to one's capacity: a child can keep a small picture and offer one flower or light a lamp, and Krishna remembers that person all day. Watching the arati in the temple gives the same benefit as performing it. Maharaj adds that professionals, housewives and students around the world follow this programme, which Srila Prabhupada made practical without compromise.

🎙 Maharaj at 65:21 (auto-transcript): “And this worship may not be elaborate. It can depend on your time. Whatever time you have, you can minimum, you should do something. At least offer a flower. Like every day, sometimes it so happens that some children, they cannot do elaborate worship. They can have a small…”

What we avoid matters as much as what we do. Maharaj names four activities - meat-eating, intoxication, illicit sex and gambling - and says each destroys one pillar of religion: mercy, austerity, cleanliness and truthfulness.

🎙 Maharaj at 67:52 (auto-transcript): “for us. Now, we discussed five things, what we are supposed to do. Now, there are certain things which you're not supposed to do and this also as important as what we're supposed to do what are the false things which you are not supposed to do now before discussing that i use…”

A diabetic takes his injections but his sugar keeps rising; the doctor finds he is eating sweets every day. In the same way the five practices have little effect if the four sinful activities continue.

🎙 Maharaj at 68:11 (auto-transcript): “use one example why whatever we do it is only of good credit when only we follow the don'ts a patient was there he went to the doctor the doctor examined him did the blood test diabetes, so you should take insulin. So the doctor gave some diabetes, some injections. He told…”

Meat-eating destroys compassion, and Maharaj says compassion and tolerance are what make human society human: nobody befriends a tiger, but anyone can befriend a cow. He also says the human body, by its intestines, digestive acid and teeth, is built like that of a plant-eater.

🎙 Maharaj at 69:58 (auto-transcript): “Meat-eating destroys mercy, compassion. It is actually compassion and tolerance which actually makes a human society human. When compassion and tolerance is not there, though we call it a society of humans, it is actually a society of animals. So why is society of animals,…”

Being vegetarian is no great thing, and plants are living too. The point is to cook pure food, offer it to Krishna and take it as prasadam, which frees one from reaction. Maharaj tells of Indians who drive a hundred kilometres abroad for lunch at an ISKCON restaurant but never visit the temple near home, and of Srila Prabhupada's remark about a movement begun from the kitchen. — “Because monkey is a vegetarian, isn't it?”

🎙 Maharaj at 72:41 (auto-transcript): “Now here, we are not just proposing that you be a vegetarian. Because monkey is a vegetarian, isn't it? What's the big thing in being vegetarian? So we are not just saying that you be a vegetarian. We actually advise that we should be krishnatarian. what is the meaning of…”

Intoxication destroys austerity, the determination to keep a vow and accept some difficulty, without which there is no progress even materially. One who depends on a substance becomes its servant.

🎙 Maharaj at 74:54 (auto-transcript): “So now after talking about this non-vegetarian being avoiding no meat or no meat is one of the leading principles. The second thing is no intoxication. Intoxication destroys the pillar of austerity. Nobody can be austere if he is intoxicated. Austerity means to follow certain…”

At a college New Year's party where Maharaj alone was not drinking, a friend sat beside him in tears, holding what he vowed was his last cigarette. Maharaj told him a vow taken while drunk means nothing, and a few days later the friend was smoking again.

🎙 Maharaj at 76:01 (auto-transcript): “Once, I remember there was a New Year's party in our college and I was the only person who was not drinking. Once, my friend came with a cigarette in hand and sat next to me and he was crying. It was New Year's Eve. He was crying and crying. I told him, what happened to you?…”

Devotees also avoid tea and coffee. Maharaj gives his account of how colonial rulers turned food crops into cash crops and built a market by first giving tea away free. He asks a coffee-loving Sanskrit professor whether his headache comes from not drinking coffee or from the habit of drinking it, and suggests herbal drinks instead.

🎙 Maharaj at 77:41 (auto-transcript): “But you find that the Hare Krishnas, we also try to avoid and even advise everyone to avoid tea and coffee also. You may say, oh why? It is very natural, no? But it has become a natural intoxicant. That is the problem. Actually, this tea and coffee was not there in this land…”

Gambling destroys truthfulness. Maharaj describes clubs in Bombay full of card players all night on Janmashtami while temples hold kirtan, and a man who told him that this was how he had celebrated.

🎙 Maharaj at 81:31 (auto-transcript): “The third one is no gambling. No gambling is also very important. Especially people have gambled, there is so much related to gambling. Especially when festivals come, people get together and start gambling. I don't know what's the position here. Especially in Bombay, during…”

Gambling means depending on what is uncertain. The most unexpected thing is death, so to put off Krishna consciousness and live for one's own enjoyment is to gamble with time.

🎙 Maharaj at 83:01 (auto-transcript): “gambling just doesn't mean playing cards or going to casinos or something like that. Gambling also means not to take a Krishna consciousness seriously. You are gambling with time. That means, gambling means what? To depend on something which is indifferent. That is called…”

Relations outside marriage destroy cleanliness of body and mind. Maharaj says television and the internet present it to the young as natural, and that it leaves emotional wounds no medicine can heal; even sacred festivals get used for it, so families should arrange wholesome alternatives such as dancing to the Hare Krishna mantra.

🎙 Maharaj at 83:41 (auto-transcript): “If you don't take a Krishna consciousness seriously. Now going further, the fourth one, illicit sex. So this has to be avoided. Because illicit sex will destroy the pillar of cleanliness. The cleanliness of the body, the physical cleanliness and mental cleanliness. Now, it…”

To anyone who finds all this hard, Maharaj says that with Krishna difficult things become easy, and the strength to follow the four principles comes from chanting. Krishna consciousness is not the end of enjoyment but complete satisfaction on four levels. — “If you have Krishna with you, difficult things become easy.”

🎙 Maharaj at 87:20 (auto-transcript): “If you have Krishna with you, difficult things become easy. If you don't have Krishna, easy things become difficult. You find thousands of people, millions of people accepting Krishna consciousness and following the four regulated principles. Where are they getting the…”

With prasadam and a regulated life, Maharaj says, devotees stay healthy and cheerful. Their faces are bright without cosmetics; he recalls a newspaper headline about saffron robes and beaming smiles.

🎙 Maharaj at 88:01 (auto-transcript): “But be sure, Krishna consciousness is the real enjoyment. It gives 100% written Krishna Prasad, you will never fall sick. Because of a regular life, you will never fall sick. Physically, 100% satisfaction. That is, you find devotees, they are more healthy and they are more…”

At worldly parties people smile artificially and on the way home the talk is all grudges, because everyone wants to appear superior. Among devotees the mood is to serve one another, and only there is the mind at rest.

🎙 Maharaj at 88:54 (auto-transcript): “So this is how. A person becomes beautiful because of being cheerful, not because of applying cosmetics. So that happens only when you are emotionally completely satisfied. So completely, mind is satisfied, 100% satisfied because you are among people who are not envious. When…”

The Gita answers every question the intellect can raise. And the soul, unfed for countless lifetimes, finally gets its food in the holy name. Maharaj closes the course by thanking the Colombo audience for attending every day. — “So, you should be happy losing suffering.”

🎙 Maharaj at 90:41 (auto-transcript): “Number three, physical, mental, intellectual. There is no philosophy equal to Christian consciousness. Bhagavad Gita is the best philosophy. There is answer to questions, answer to all the questions which you can ask. Intellectually, a person is 100% satisfied when he reads…”

Maharaj invites questions before the closing chanting and takes five.

🎙 Maharaj at 93:14 (auto-transcript): “Any questions? Any comments before we chant Hare Krishna mantra? I hope you have done the homework. How many of you have done the homework? Okay, most of you have done the homework. So we will chant Hare Krishna mantra at the end. So some announcements are there. By the time,…”

A listener asks why Lord Buddha, an incarnation of Krishna, taught non-violence while Krishna told Arjuna to fight. Maharaj answers on two levels.

🎙 Question from the floor at 93:47 (auto-transcript): “Buddha was the reincarnation of Krishna. We understand. And where Lord Buddha teaches non-violence, where Krishna is teaching about to kill the enemies to Arjuna. Nice question. Lord Krishna is teaching violence. Buddha taught non-violence. And the devotees of both of them do…”

children.topic: Buddha came to stop animal slaughter
children.note:
Citing Jayadeva Goswami's prayer, Maharaj says animals were being killed in the name of Vedic sacrifice just to please the tongue, and the Lord came as Buddha to stop that misuse. Asked about God, Buddha kept silent, and in Maharaj's telling that silence was taken to mean there is no God.

🎙 Maharaj at 94:41 (auto-transcript): “So I answered the question in two levels. Number one is about Buddha. Krishna Incarnationist Buddha, it is said in the Jai Daigo Swami Stotra that how Pashukhatham, he could not tolerate people. Nindasi yagnami dhe raha pashukhatham, snabaiti pashyasi, samithasam bhavatam,…”

A mother who disciplines her child does good, while one who never corrects him spoils him. Krishna telling Arjuna to fight is like a surgeon cutting open a patient to remove a cancer. — “So we should understand the ultimate purpose rather than the activity itself.”

🎙 Maharaj at 96:50 (auto-transcript): “Now going further, your question is about Krishna is recommending violence. Violence is not bad, but the purpose for which the violence is used, that is important. Actually, I think this word is bad, provided it is used properly. Non-violence for a bad purpose is bad.…”

children.topic: Q2 · Gita and Bhagavatam: the difference?
children.note:
The question itself is not audible; Maharaj summarises the difference between the two books.

🎙 Question from the floor at 98:18 (auto-transcript): “I will summarize the difference between them. Bhagavad Gita, it is by Krishna, spoken by Krishna. Srimad Bhagavatam is spoken about Krishna. Now, Srimad Bhagavad Gita talks about what to do, what to do, the instruction. And Bhagavatam talks about how to do. Bhagavad Gita,…”

The Gita is spoken by Krishna and tells what to do; the Bhagavatam is spoken about Krishna and shows how, through devotees such as Bhishma, Kunti, the gopis and Pariksit. The Bhagavatam begins where the Gita ends, with 18,000 verses to the Gita's 700; the Gita is philosophy, the Bhagavatam the taste of living it.

🎙 Maharaj at 98:23 (auto-transcript): “Bhagavad Gita, it is by Krishna, spoken by Krishna. Srimad Bhagavatam is spoken about Krishna. Now, Srimad Bhagavad Gita talks about what to do, what to do, the instruction. And Bhagavatam talks about how to do. Bhagavad Gita, Krishna said, think of me, then the Bhagavatam…”

Maharaj says he holds some points back so they can come out more deeply in answer to a question like this one.

🎙 Question from the floor at 100:48 (auto-transcript): “Can you explain about Akarma a little bit more? Certain things I intentionally don't speak in the course because I want it is spoken as an answer to a question that goes more deeper. That is why I wait for those questions. Let us talk about starting from sleep. Sleep is also…”

He walks through a day: sleeping so as to be fresh for service, bathing because one cannot stand unclean before Krishna, chanting and reading as armour for the battlefield of the day, taking prasadam, earning to buy flowers and clothes for Krishna, and caring for a family who are His servants. With Krishna in the centre, all of it is akarma; without Him, each of these becomes a cause of frustration.

🎙 Maharaj at 101:14 (auto-transcript): “Let us talk about starting from sleep. Sleep is also an activity. A devotee when he sleeps, though it is the most ignorant activity, sleeping is actually more of ignorance. Even that activity is akarma. Why? Because devotee sleeps so that morning he can be fresh to serve…”

Throw stones into a still pond at different points and the ripples clash and look ugly; throw them at the same point and the circles grow more beautiful. So it is when every activity has Krishna as its centre.

🎙 Maharaj at 105:23 (auto-transcript): “Like you throw a stone on a pond, very calm water is there in the pond, nice ripples come. You throw another stone and the center is somewhere else, then ripples come and they clash and it becomes very ugly. But if you throw the stone at the same point, the ripples become…”

A listener asks how the movement started. Maharaj says it may look like a modern international organisation, but its roots are in Krishna's teachings in the Gita.

🎙 Question from the floor at 105:56 (auto-transcript): “I can just know how this whole concept of this concept started. Okay. We know about Sri Prabhupada, but still we should be having some guru and we want to know how to do it all. Okay. It's called, it seems to be modernised organisation with high tech management and so on,…”

The teachings came through Lord Caitanya and the six Goswamis, then Srila Bhaktivinoda Thakura and his son Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Thakura, who met Srila Prabhupada in 1922 and asked him to teach in the English-speaking world. Srila Prabhupada prepared for decades and first tried in India.

🎙 Maharaj at 106:42 (auto-transcript): “So in the line of Sri Chaitanya Mahapurou teachings, there appeared many Acharyas. First disciples of Sri Chaitanya Mahapurou were known as Shadgo Swamis. The teachings of Shatgo Swamis were delivered to us in the modern world, the recent past by Shilabhakti Nod Thakur.…”

Given passage on a cargo ship that sailed from Calcutta and first stopped at Colombo, Srila Prabhupada suffered two heart attacks at sea and then, Maharaj relates, dreamt of Krishna assuring him of his mission. After early struggle his chanting and affection drew his first followers; he brought twelve of them to India, and the movement grew around teaching the Gita and Bhagavatam, distributing books and opening temples.

🎙 Maharaj at 108:08 (auto-transcript): “me take this knowledge to the vessel. Sri Mali Maharaj, she was the Managing Director of Steamship Company at that time. So somehow Prabhupada convinced her to give a ticket to go to America. It is a cargo vessel called Passages of the Road. So Prabhupada go to the ship in…”

children.topic: Q5 · Krishna as time, the destroyer?
children.note:
The last question is about Krishna's statement that He is time, the destroyer of the worlds.

🎙 Question from the floor at 111:15 (auto-transcript): “So one last question. I am the destroyer of the world. Krishna says that I am time. The most powerful feature in the entire world is time. They mean when time bombs and all these things, but ultimately time is a destroyer. One thing you cannot hold on, that is this watch. It…”

Nobody can stop the watch; each sunrise and sunset is one day nearer to death, while we keep our eyes closed. For a devotee time has no hold: like a student who studies well and moves up at the end of the year while another's year is wasted, the devotee uses life to go back to the spiritual world instead of taking birth again. The best use of time is Krishna's service.

🎙 Maharaj at 111:55 (auto-transcript): “One thing you cannot hold on, that is this watch. It goes on. You cannot stop it. How can you hold? You cannot hold it. It just goes straight. The most powerful thing in this world is time. It is pushing everybody towards death. It is just pushing towards death. Just imagine…”
